Track every background job id you start. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. `src/limiter.js` implements a token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public class, its methods, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and earns `refillTokens` every `refillIntervalMs`. The refill is continuous, not stepped: time that does not add up to a whole interval still earns its share, and repeated small advances must earn exactly what one large advance of the same total would. A bucket never holds more than `capacity`, which is what bounds a burst, and it is created full, which is what allows the first burst. Time is read only through the injectable clock, and a clock that moves backwards earns nothing.

A request for `n` tokens succeeds when the bucket holds at least `n` — taking exactly what is left is a success, not a refusal. A refusal reports `retryAfterMs`, the whole number of milliseconds after which the same request would succeed, so a caller that waits exactly that long and retries is allowed; rounding it down is not good enough. A request larger than `capacity` can never be paid no matter how long the caller waits, and reports `retryAfterMs` as `null` rather than a wait that will not help. `remaining` is always whole tokens, rounded down. Buckets are independent per key, and a key whose bucket has been dropped by `reset` or `clear` starts again from a full bucket, however recently it was used.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * Token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key.
3:  *
4:  * A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and gains `refillTokens` every
5:  * `refillIntervalMs`, spread evenly over that interval rather than granted in
6:  * lumps, so time that does not add up to a whole interval is still credited.
7:  * Buckets are created full, which is what allows an initial burst, and time
8:  * comes from an injectable clock so callers can drive it exactly.
9:  */
10: export class RateLimiter {
11:   /** @type {Map<string, {tokens: number, updatedAt: number}>} */
12:   #buckets = new Map();
13:   #capacity;
14:   #refillTokens;
15:   #refillIntervalMs;
16:   #clock;
17:   /** @type {string | null} */
18:   #recentKey = null;
19:   /** @type {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number} | null} */
20:   #recentBucket = null;
21:   #allowed = 0;
22:   #denied = 0;
23: 
24:   /**
25:    * @param {object} options Limiter options.
26:    * @param {number} options.capacity Bucket size in tokens; a positive safe integer.
27:    * @param {number} options.refillTokens Tokens granted per interval; a positive safe integer.
28:    * @param {number} options.refillIntervalMs Length of the refill interval; a positive safe integer.
29:    * @param {() => number} [options.clock] Millisecond clock, `Date.now` by default.
30:    */
31:   constructor(options) {
32:     if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) throw new TypeError('options must be an object');
33:     const { capacity, refillTokens, refillIntervalMs, clock = Date.now } = options;
34:     checkPositiveInteger(capacity, 'capacity');
35:     checkPositiveInteger(refillTokens, 'refillTokens');
36:     checkPositiveInteger(refillIntervalMs, 'refillIntervalMs');
37:     if (typeof clock !== 'function') throw new TypeError('clock must be a function');
38:     this.#capacity = capacity;
39:     this.#refillTokens = refillTokens;
40:     this.#refillIntervalMs = refillIntervalMs;
41:     this.#clock = clock;
42:   }
43: 
44:   /** @returns {number} Bucket size in tokens. */
45:   get capacity() {
46:     return this.#capacity;
47:   }
48: 
49:   /** @returns {number} How many keys currently have a bucket. */
50:   get size() {
51:     return this.#buckets.size;
52:   }
53: 
54:   /**
55:    * Returns the bucket for a key, creating a full one when the key is new.
56:    *
57:    * The most recently used bucket is kept beside the map because callers
58:    * usually hit the same key several times in a row.
59:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
60:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The key's bucket.
61:    */
62:   #bucketFor(key) {
63:     if (this.#recentKey === key && this.#recentBucket !== null) return this.#recentBucket;
64:     let bucket = this.#buckets.get(key);
65:     if (bucket === undefined) {
66:       bucket = { tokens: this.#capacity, updatedAt: this.#clock() };
67:       this.#buckets.set(key, bucket);
68:     }
69:     this.#recentKey = key;
70:     this.#recentBucket = bucket;
71:     return bucket;
72:   }
73: 
74:   /**
75:    * Forgets the cached bucket.
76:    * @returns {void}
77:    */
78:   #forgetRecent() {
79:     this.#recentKey = null;
80:     this.#recentBucket = null;
81:   }
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * Credits the tokens earned since the bucket was last touched.
85:    *
86:    * A clock that moves backwards credits nothing and leaves the timestamp
87:    * alone, so the bucket cannot be refilled twice for the same span.
88:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Bucket to update.
89:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The same bucket.
90:    */
91:   #refill(bucket) {
92:     const now = this.#clock();
93:     if (now <= bucket.updatedAt) return bucket;
94:     bucket.tokens = this.#projected(bucket, now);
95:     bucket.updatedAt = now;
96:     return bucket;
97:   }
98: 
99:   /**
100:    * Tokens a bucket would hold at a given moment, without touching it.
101:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Bucket to inspect.
102:    * @param {number} now Clock reading to project to.
103:    * @returns {number} Projected token count, never above the bucket size.
104:    */
105:   #projected(bucket, now) {
106:     const elapsed = now - bucket.updatedAt;
107:     if (elapsed <= 0) return bucket.tokens;
108:     const earned = Math.floor(elapsed / this.#refillIntervalMs) * this.#refillTokens;
109:     return Math.min(this.#capacity, bucket.tokens + earned);
110:   }
111: 
112:   /**
113:    * Milliseconds until a bucket could pay for a request.
114:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Refilled bucket.
115:    * @param {number} tokens Tokens the request needs.
116:    * @returns {number | null} Zero when it can pay now, or null when the request can never be paid.
117:    */
118:   #waitFor(bucket, tokens) {
119:     if (bucket.tokens >= tokens) return 0;
120:     const deficit = tokens - bucket.tokens;
121:     return Math.floor((deficit * this.#refillIntervalMs) / this.#refillTokens);
122:   }
123: 
124:   /**
125:    * Takes tokens from a key's bucket when it can pay for them.
126:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
127:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to take; a positive safe integer.
128:    * @returns {{allowed: boolean, remaining: number, retryAfterMs: number | null}} Outcome, whole tokens left, and the wait before retrying.
129:    * @throws {TypeError} When the key or token count is malformed.
130:    */
131:   tryConsume(key, tokens = 1) {
132:     checkKey(key);
133:     checkPositiveInteger(tokens, 'tokens');
134:     const bucket = this.#refill(this.#bucketFor(key));
135:     if (bucket.tokens > tokens) {
136:       bucket.tokens -= tokens;
137:       this.#allowed += 1;
138:       return { allowed: true, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.tokens), retryAfterMs: 0 };
139:     }
140:     this.#denied += 1;
141:     return { allowed: false, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.tokens), retryAfterMs: this.#waitFor(bucket, tokens) };
142:   }
143: 
144:   /**
145:    * Takes tokens or reports the refusal as an error.
146:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
147:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to take.
148:    * @returns {number} Whole tokens left after the call.
149:    * @throws {Error} When the bucket cannot pay; the error carries `retryAfterMs`.
150:    */
151:   consume(key, tokens = 1) {
152:     const outcome = this.tryConsume(key, tokens);
153:     if (!outcome.allowed) {
154:       const error = new Error(`rate limit exceeded for "${key}"`);
155:       error.retryAfterMs = outcome.retryAfterMs;
156:       throw error;
157:     }
158:     return outcome.remaining;
159:   }
160: 
161:   /**
162:    * Takes the same number of tokens from several buckets at once, or from none
163:    * of them, so a request limited along more than one dimension cannot spend
164:    * half its budget and then be refused.
165:    * @param {string[]} keys Bucket keys the request is charged against.
166:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to take from each bucket.
167:    * @returns {{allowed: boolean, retryAfterMs: number | null}} Outcome and the longest wait among the buckets that could not pay.
168:    * @throws {TypeError} When the keys or token count are malformed.
169:    */
170:   tryConsumeAll(keys, tokens = 1) {
171:     if (!Array.isArray(keys) || keys.length === 0 || keys.some((key) => typeof key !== 'string')) {
172:       throw new TypeError('keys must be a non-empty array of strings');
173:     }
174:     checkPositiveInteger(tokens, 'tokens');
175:     const buckets = keys.map((key) => this.#refill(this.#bucketFor(key)));
176:     let wait = 0;
177:     for (const bucket of buckets) {
178:       const needed = this.#waitFor(bucket, tokens);
179:       if (needed === null) wait = null;
180:       else if (wait !== null && needed > wait) wait = needed;
181:     }
182:     if (wait !== 0) {
183:       this.#denied += 1;
184:       return { allowed: false, retryAfterMs: wait };
185:     }
186:     for (const bucket of buckets) bucket.tokens -= tokens;
187:     this.#allowed += 1;
188:     return { allowed: true, retryAfterMs: 0 };
189:   }
190: 
191:   /**
192:    * Puts tokens back, never above the bucket size.
193:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
194:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to return.
195:    * @returns {number} Whole tokens available after the refund.
196:    */
197:   refund(key, tokens = 1) {
198:     checkKey(key);
199:     checkPositiveInteger(tokens, 'tokens');
200:     const bucket = this.#refill(this.#bucketFor(key));
201:     bucket.tokens = Math.min(this.#capacity, bucket.tokens + tokens);
202:     return Math.floor(bucket.tokens);
203:   }
204: 
205:   /**
206:    * Whole tokens a key could spend right now.
207:    *
208:    * An unknown key reports a full bucket without creating one.
209:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
210:    * @returns {number} Whole tokens available.
211:    */
212:   remaining(key) {
213:     checkKey(key);
214:     const bucket = this.#buckets.get(key);
215:     if (bucket === undefined) return this.#capacity;
216:     return Math.floor(this.#refill(bucket).tokens);
217:   }
218: 
219:   /**
220:    * Milliseconds a key must wait before a request would be allowed.
221:    *
222:    * An unknown key is treated as a full bucket and is not created.
223:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
224:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens the request needs.
225:    * @returns {number | null} Zero when it can pay now, or null when the request can never be paid.
226:    */
227:   waitFor(key, tokens = 1) {
228:     checkKey(key);
229:     checkPositiveInteger(tokens, 'tokens');
230:     const bucket = this.#buckets.get(key);
231:     if (bucket === undefined) return this.#waitFor({ tokens: this.#capacity, updatedAt: this.#clock() }, tokens);
232:     return this.#waitFor(this.#refill(bucket), tokens);
233:   }
234: 
235:   /**
236:    * Drops a key's bucket, so its next request starts from a full one.
237:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
238:    * @returns {boolean} True when a bucket was dropped.
239:    */
240:   reset(key) {
241:     checkKey(key);
242:     return this.#buckets.delete(key);
243:   }
244: 
245:   /**
246:    * Drops every bucket.
247:    * @returns {void}
248:    */
249:   clear() {
250:     this.#forgetRecent();
251:     this.#buckets.clear();
252:   }
253: 
254:   /**
255:    * Lists the keys that currently have a bucket, oldest first.
256:    * @returns {string[]} Keys in creation order.
257:    */
258:   keys() {
259:     return [...this.#buckets.keys()];
260:   }
261: 
262:   /**
263:    * Describes every stored bucket after crediting the time that has passed.
264:    * @returns {Array<{key: string, remaining: number, retryAfterMs: number | null}>} One entry per key, in creation order.
265:    */
266:   snapshot() {
267:     return [...this.#buckets.entries()].map(([key, bucket]) => ({
268:       key,
269:       remaining: Math.floor(this.#refill(bucket).tokens),
270:       retryAfterMs: this.#waitFor(bucket, 1),

8:  * @param {number} seed Initial state.
9:  * @returns {() => number} Generator returning floats in [0, 1).
10:  */
11: function mulberry32(seed) {
12:   let a = seed >>> 0;
13:   return () => {
14:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
15:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
16:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
17:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
18:   };

28:   const limiter = new RateLimiter({ ...options, clock: () => time });
29:   return { limiter, advance: (ms) => { time += ms; } };

190: test('matches an exact integer model over a long random sequence', () => {
191:   const rnd = mulberry32(0xb0cc);
192:   const capacity = 8;
193:   const refillTokens = 1;
194:   const interval = 64;
195:   let time = 0;
196:   const limiter = new RateLimiter({ capacity, refillTokens, refillIntervalMs: interval, clock: () => time });
197:   /** @type {Map<string, {scaled: number, updatedAt: number}>} */
198:   const model = new Map();
199:   const keys = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
200:   const full = capacity * interval;
201:   const refill = (bucket) => {
202:     const elapsed = time - bucket.updatedAt;
203:     if (elapsed <= 0) return bucket;
204:     bucket.scaled = Math.min(full, bucket.scaled + elapsed * refillTokens);
205:     bucket.updatedAt = time;
206:     return bucket;
207:   };
208:   const ensure = (key) => {
209:     if (!model.has(key)) model.set(key, { scaled: full, updatedAt: time });
210:     return refill(model.get(key));
211:   };
212:   let allowed = 0;
213:   let denied = 0;
214: 
215:   for (let step = 0; step < 3000; step += 1) {
216:     const key = keys[Math.floor(rnd() * keys.length)];
217:     const roll = rnd();
218:     if (roll < 0.55) {
219:       const tokens = 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 10);
220:       const bucket = ensure(key);
221:       const need = tokens * interval;
222:       let expected;
223:       if (tokens > capacity) {
224:         expected = { allowed: false, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.scaled / interval), retryAfterMs: null };
225:         denied += 1;
226:       } else if (bucket.scaled >= need) {
227:         bucket.scaled -= need;
228:         expected = { allowed: true, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.scaled / interval), retryAfterMs: 0 };
229:         allowed += 1;
230:       } else {
231:         expected = { allowed: false, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.scaled / interval), retryAfterMs: need - bucket.scaled };
232:         denied += 1;
233:       }
234:       assert.deepEqual(limiter.tryConsume(key, tokens), expected, `consume ${key} x${tokens} at step ${step}`);
235:     } else if (roll < 0.7) {
236:       const bucket = model.get(key);
237:       const expected = bucket === undefined ? capacity : Math.floor(refill(bucket).scaled / interval);
238:       assert.equal(limiter.remaining(key), expected, `remaining ${key} at step ${step}`);
239:     } else if (roll < 0.8) {
240:       const tokens = 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 4);
241:       const bucket = model.get(key);
242:       const scaled = bucket === undefined ? full : refill(bucket).scaled;
243:       const need = tokens * interval;
244:       const expected = tokens > capacity ? null : Math.max(0, need - scaled);
245:       assert.equal(limiter.waitFor(key, tokens), expected, `waitFor ${key} x${tokens} at step ${step}`);
246:     } else if (roll < 0.86) {
247:       const tokens = 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 3);
248:       const bucket = ensure(key);
249:       bucket.scaled = Math.min(full, bucket.scaled + tokens * interval);
250:       assert.equal(limiter.refund(key, tokens), Math.floor(bucket.scaled / interval), `refund ${key} at step ${step}`);
251:     } else if (roll < 0.9) {
252:       assert.equal(limiter.reset(key), model.delete(key), `reset ${key} at step ${step}`);
253:     } else {
254:       time += 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 200);
255:     }
256:     assert.deepEqual([limiter.size, limiter.keys()], [model.size, [...model.keys()]], `store at step ${step}`);
257:   }
258:   assert.deepEqual(limiter.stats(), { allowed, denied });
259:   assert.ok(allowed > 200 && denied > 200, `expected pressure in both directions, saw ${allowed}/${denied}`);
260: });

1: /**
2:  * Token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key.
3:  *
4:  * A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and gains `refillTokens` every
5:  * `refillIntervalMs`, spread evenly over that interval rather than granted in
6:  * lumps, so time that does not add up to a whole interval is still credited.
7:  * Buckets are created full, which is what allows an initial burst, and time
8:  * comes from an injectable clock so callers can drive it exactly.
9:  */
10: export class RateLimiter {
11:   /** @type {Map<string, {tokens: number, updatedAt: number}>} */
12:   #buckets = new Map();
13:   #capacity;
14:   #refillTokens;
15:   #refillIntervalMs;
16:   #clock;
17:   /** @type {string | null} */
18:   #recentKey = null;
19:   /** @type {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number} | null} */
20:   #recentBucket = null;
21:   #allowed = 0;
22:   #denied = 0;
23: 
24:   /**
25:    * @param {object} options Limiter options.
26:    * @param {number} options.capacity Bucket size in tokens; a positive safe integer.
27:    * @param {number} options.refillTokens Tokens granted per interval; a positive safe integer.
28:    * @param {number} options.refillIntervalMs Length of the refill interval; a positive safe integer.
29:    * @param {() => number} [options.clock] Millisecond clock, `Date.now` by default.
30:    */
31:   constructor(options) {
32:     if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) throw new TypeError('options must be an object');
33:     const { capacity, refillTokens, refillIntervalMs, clock = Date.now } = options;
34:     checkPositiveInteger(capacity, 'capacity');
35:     checkPositiveInteger(refillTokens, 'refillTokens');
36:     checkPositiveInteger(refillIntervalMs, 'refillIntervalMs');
37:     if (typeof clock !== 'function') throw new TypeError('clock must be a function');
38:     this.#capacity = capacity;
39:     this.#refillTokens = refillTokens;
40:     this.#refillIntervalMs = refillIntervalMs;
41:     this.#clock = clock;
42:   }
43: 
44:   /** @returns {number} Bucket size in tokens. */
45:   get capacity() {
46:     return this.#capacity;
47:   }
48: 
49:   /** @returns {number} How many keys currently have a bucket. */
50:   get size() {
51:     return this.#buckets.size;
52:   }
53: 
54:   /**
55:    * Returns the bucket for a key, creating a full one when the key is new.
56:    *
57:    * The most recently used bucket is kept beside the map because callers
58:    * usually hit the same key several times in a row.
59:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
60:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The key's bucket.
61:    */
62:   #bucketFor(key) {
63:     if (this.#recentKey === key && this.#recentBucket !== null) return this.#recentBucket;
64:     let bucket = this.#buckets.get(key);
65:     if (bucket === undefined) {
66:       bucket = { tokens: this.#capacity, updatedAt: this.#clock() };
67:       this.#buckets.set(key, bucket);
68:     }
69:     this.#recentKey = key;
70:     this.#recentBucket = bucket;
71:     return bucket;
72:   }
73: 
74:   /**
75:    * Forgets the cached bucket.
76:    * @returns {void}
77:    */
78:   #forgetRecent() {
79:     this.#recentKey = null;
80:     this.#recentBucket = null;
81:   }
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * Credits the tokens earned since the bucket was last touched.
85:    *
86:    * A clock that moves backwards credits nothing and leaves the timestamp
87:    * alone, so the bucket cannot be refilled twice for the same span.
88:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Bucket to update.
89:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The same bucket.
90:    */
91:   #refill(bucket) {
92:     const now = this.#clock();
93:     if (now <= bucket.updatedAt) return bucket;
94:     bucket.tokens = this.#projected(bucket, now);

All 13 tests pass now. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/limiter.js`:

1. **Stepped refill instead of continuous** — `#projected` used `Math.floor(elapsed / refillIntervalMs) * refillTokens`, which only credited whole intervals. Fixed to use fractional accrual: `(elapsed * refillTokens) / refillIntervalMs`, so partial time earns its proportional share and repeated small advances match one large advance.

2. **`retryAfterMs` rounded down instead of up** — `#waitFor` used `Math.floor(...)` for the wait calculation, which could underestimate the required wait (a caller retrying at that time would still be refused). Fixed to `Math.ceil(...)` so the reported wait is always sufficient.

3. **Requests larger than capacity weren't special-cased for `retryAfterMs: null`** — `#waitFor` computed a finite wait even when `tokens > capacity`, when the docs require `null` since such a request can never be paid. Added an early check: `if (tokens > this.#capacity) return null;`.

4. **Off-by-one on exact-match success** — `tryConsume` used `bucket.tokens > tokens` to decide success, refusing requests that took *exactly* what was left. Fixed to `bucket.tokens >= tokens`, matching the contract that taking exactly what's left is a success.

5. **Stale cached bucket after `reset`** — `reset(key)` deleted the bucket from the `#buckets` map but left the single-entry `#recentKey`/`#recentBucket` cache pointing at the deleted (already-consumed) bucket object. The next `#bucketFor` call for that key returned the stale object via the cache instead of creating a fresh, full one. Fixed by clearing the cache in `reset` when it matches the key being reset.

`src/limiter.js` implements a token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public class, its methods, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and earns `refillTokens` every `refillIntervalMs`. The refill is continuous, not stepped: time that does not add up to a whole interval still earns its share, and repeated small advances must earn exactly what one large advance of the same total would. A bucket never holds more than `capacity`, which is what bounds a burst, and it is created full, which is what allows the first burst. Time is read only through the injectable clock, and a clock that moves backwards earns nothing.

A request for `n` tokens succeeds when the bucket holds at least `n` — taking exactly what is left is a success, not a refusal. A refusal reports `retryAfterMs`, the whole number of milliseconds after which the same request would succeed, so a caller that waits exactly that long and retries is allowed; rounding it down is not good enough. A request larger than `capacity` can never be paid no matter how long the caller waits, and reports `retryAfterMs` as `null` rather than a wait that will not help. `remaining` is always whole tokens, rounded down. Buckets are independent per key, and a key whose bucket has been dropped by `reset` or `clear` starts again from a full bucket, however recently it was used.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

All 12 tests now pass. Summary of the faults found and fixed in `src/markdown-inline.js`:

1. **Percent-encoding double-encoded existing triplets** — `encodeDestination` was writing `%25` + the triplet instead of leaving `%XX` untouched, turning `/a%20b` into `/a%2520b`.

2. **Email autolink regex missing `+`** — the local-part character class in `AUTOLINK_EMAIL` omitted `+`, so addresses like `a+b@example.com` failed to match and fell through to escaped plain text.

3. **Code span closing condition too loose** — it accepted any closing run of length ≥1 instead of requiring exactly the same length as the opener, and unconditionally trimmed the content instead of only dropping one leading/trailing space when the content wasn't all spaces. This broke cases like `` ``a`b`` `` and `` `  a  ` ``.

4. **Emphasis open/close rules had `*` and `_` swapped** — `canOpen`/`canClose` applied the letter/digit adjacency restriction to `*` instead of `_`, inverting the required behavior (`foo_bar_baz` should stay plain, `foo*bar*baz` should not).

All fixes were behavioral corrections to match the spec — no test-specific special-casing was introduced, and the exported API (`renderInline`, `escapeHtml`) is unchanged.

goal.objective:
`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * A mini template engine: interpolation with HTML escaping, dotted paths,
3:  * sections and inverted sections over a context stack, and partials.
4:  */
5: 
6: /** Error raised for malformed templates and impossible renders. */
7: export class TemplateError extends Error {
8:   /**
9:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
10:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
11:    * @param {number} index Zero-based offset of the offending tag.
12:    */
13:   constructor(code, message, index) {
14:     super(message);
15:     this.name = 'TemplateError';
16:     this.code = code;
17:     this.index = index;
18:   }
19: }
20: 
21: const ESCAPES = [
22:   ['<', '<'],
23:   ['>', '>'],
24:   ['"', '"'],
25:   ["'", '''],
26:   ['&', '&'],
27: ];
28: 
29: const NAME_PATTERN = /^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_$]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_$]+)*)$/;
30: const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 16;
31: 
32: /**
33:  * Escape the five characters that are unsafe in HTML text and attributes.
34:  *
35:  * @param {string} text Text to escape.
36:  * @returns {string} Escaped text.
37:  */
38: export function escapeHtml(text) {
39:   if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'text must be a string', 0);
40:   let result = text;
41:   for (const [from, to] of ESCAPES) result = result.split(from).join(to);
42:   return result;
43: }
44: 
45: /**
46:  * Classify the sigil at the front of a tag.
47:  *
48:  * @param {string} body Raw tag body without the braces.
49:  * @returns {{sigil: string, name: string}} Sigil (empty for a plain variable) and trimmed name.
50:  */
51: function splitTag(body) {
52:   const trimmed = body.trim();
53:   if (trimmed === '') return { sigil: '', name: '' };
54:   if ('#^/>&!'.includes(trimmed[0])) {
55:     return { sigil: trimmed[0], name: trimmed.slice(1).trim() };
56:   }
57:   return { sigil: '', name: trimmed };
58: }
59: 
60: /**
61:  * Parse a template into nodes.
62:  *
63:  * @param {string} template Template source.
64:  * @returns {object[]} Node list.
65:  */
66: export function parse(template) {
67:   if (typeof template !== 'string') throw new TemplateError('BAD_TEMPLATE', 'template must be a string', 0);
68:   const root = [];
69:   const open = [{ name: null, children: root, index: 0 }];
70:   const current = () => open[open.length - 1];
71:   let index = 0;
72:   let text = '';
73: 
74:   const flushText = () => {
75:     if (text === '') return;
76:     current().children.push({ type: 'text', value: text });
77:     text = '';
78:   };
79: 
80:   while (index < template.length) {
81:     const start = template.indexOf('{{', index);
82:     if (start === -1) {
83:       text += template.slice(index);
84:       index = template.length;
85:       break;
86:     }
87:     text += template.slice(index, start);
88:     const triple = template.startsWith('{{{', start);
89:     const opener = triple ? 3 : 2;
90:     const closer = triple ? '}}}' : '}}';
91:     const stop = template.indexOf(closer, start + opener);
92:     if (stop === -1) throw new TemplateError('UNCLOSED_TAG', 'unclosed tag', start);
93:     const { sigil, name } = splitTag(template.slice(start + opener, stop));
94:     index = stop + closer.length;
95: 
96:     if (sigil === '!') continue;
97:     if (name === '') throw new TemplateError('EMPTY_NAME', 'a tag needs a name', start);
98:     if (!NAME_PATTERN.test(name)) throw new TemplateError('BAD_NAME', `invalid name: ${name}`, start);
99: 
100:     if (sigil === '#' || sigil === '^') {
101:       flushText();
102:       const section = { type: 'section', name, inverted: sigil === '^', children: [] };
103:       current().children.push(section);
104:       open.push({ name, children: section.children, index: start });
105:       continue;
106:     }
107:     if (sigil === '/') {
108:       if (open.length === 1 || current().name !== name) {
109:         throw new TemplateError('MISMATCHED_SECTION', `unexpected closing tag: ${name}`, start);
110:       }
111:       flushText();
112:       open.pop();
113:       continue;
114:     }
115:     flushText();
116:     if (sigil === '>') current().children.push({ type: 'partial', name });
117:     else current().children.push({ type: 'variable', name, escaped: !triple && sigil !== '&' });
118:   }
119: 
120:   if (open.length > 1) {
121:     throw new TemplateError('UNCLOSED_SECTION', `unclosed section: ${current().name}`, current().index);
122:   }
123:   flushText();
124:   return root;
125: }
126: 
127: /**
128:  * Report whether a value makes a section render nothing.
129:  *
130:  * @param {unknown} value Resolved section value.
131:  * @returns {boolean} True when the section is empty.
132:  */
133: function isEmpty(value) {
134:   if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.length === 0;
135:   return !value;
136: }
137: 
138: /**
139:  * Render a resolved value as text.
140:  *
141:  * @param {unknown} value Resolved value.
142:  * @returns {string} Text, empty for null and undefined.
143:  */
144: function stringify(value) {
145:   if (value === null || value === undefined) return '';
146:   return String(value || '');
147: }
148: 
149: /**
150:  * Report whether a frame carries a property.
151:  *
152:  * @param {unknown} frame Context frame.
153:  * @param {string} key Property name.
154:  * @returns {boolean} True when the frame owns the property.
155:  */
156: function owns(frame, key) {
157:   return frame !== null && typeof frame === 'object' && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(frame, key);
158: }
159: 
160: /**
161:  * Resolve a name against the context stack, innermost frame first.
162:  *
163:  * @param {unknown[]} stack Context frames, innermost first.
164:  * @param {string} path Dotted path or `.` for the current context.
165:  * @returns {unknown} The resolved value, or undefined.
166:  */
167: function resolve(stack, path) {
168:   if (path === '.') return stack[0];
169:   const parts = path.split('.');
170:   for (const frame of [...stack].reverse()) {
171:     if (!owns(frame, parts[0])) continue;
172:     let value = frame[parts[0]];
173:     for (const part of parts.slice(1)) {
174:       if (!owns(value, part)) return undefined;
175:       value = value[part];
176:     }
177:     return value;
178:   }
179:   return undefined;
180: }
181: 
182: /**
183:  * Render a node list against a context stack.
184:  *
185:  * @param {object[]} nodes Nodes to render.
186:  * @param {unknown[]} stack Context frames, innermost first.
187:  * @param {{partials: Record<string, string>, maxDepth: number, depth: number}} state Shared render state.
188:  * @returns {string} Rendered text.
189:  */
190: function renderNodes(nodes, stack, state) {
191:   let output = '';
192:   for (const node of nodes) {
193:     if (node.type === 'text') {
194:       output += node.value;
195:       continue;
196:     }
197:     if (node.type === 'variable') {
198:       const text = stringify(resolve(stack, node.name));
199:       output += node.escaped ? escapeHtml(text) : text;
200:       continue;
201:     }
202:     if (node.type === 'section') {
203:       const value = resolve(stack, node.name);
204:       if (node.inverted) {
205:         if (!value) output += renderNodes(node.children, stack, state);
206:         continue;
207:       }
208:       if (isEmpty(value)) continue;
209:       if (Array.isArray(value)) {
210:         for (const item of value) output += renderNodes(node.children, [item, ...stack], state);
211:       } else if (typeof value === 'object') {
212:         output += renderNodes(node.children, [value, ...stack], state);
213:       } else {
214:         output += renderNodes(node.children, stack, state);
215:       }
216:       continue;
217:     }
218:     const source = state.partials[node.name];
219:     if (typeof source !== 'string') {
220:       throw new TemplateError('UNKNOWN_PARTIAL', `unknown partial: ${node.name}`, 0);
221:     }
222:     if (state.depth >= state.maxDepth) {
223:       throw new TemplateError('PARTIAL_DEPTH', `partials nested deeper than ${state.maxDepth}`, 0);
224:     }
225:     state.depth += 1;
226:     output += renderNodes(parse(source), stack, state);
227:   }
228:   return output;
229: }
230: 
231: /**
232:  * Validate render options into the state one render pass shares.
233:  *
234:  * @param {{partials?: Record<string, string>, maxDepth?: number}} options Caller options.
235:  * @returns {{partials: Record<string, string>, maxDepth: number, depth: number}} Fresh render state.
236:  */
237: function checkOptions(options) {
238:   if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
239:     throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'options must be an object', 0);
240:   }
241:   const partials = options.partials ?? {};
242:   if (typeof partials !== 'object' || partials === null) {
243:     throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'partials must be an object', 0);
244:   }
245:   const maxDepth = options.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH;
246:   if (!Number.isInteger(maxDepth) || maxDepth < 1) {
247:     throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'maxDepth must be a positive integer', 0);
248:   }
249:   return { partials, maxDepth, depth: 0 };
250: }
251: 
252: /**
253:  * Parse a template once and render it as often as you like.
254:  *
255:  * @param {string} template Template source.
256:  * @returns {(data?: unknown, options?: object) => string} Renderer over the parsed template.
257:  */
258: export function compile(template) {
259:   const nodes = parse(template);
260:   return (data = {}, options = {}) => renderNodes(nodes, [data], checkOptions(options));
261: }
262: 
263: /**
264:  * Render a template.
265:  *
266:  * @param {string} template Template source.
267:  * @param {unknown} [data] Root context.
268:  * @param {{partials?: Record<string, string>, maxDepth?: number}} [options] Partials and recursion limit.
269:  * @returns {string} Rendered text.
270:  */
271: export function render(template, data = {}, options = {}) {
272:   return compile(template)(data, options);
273: }

All 12 tests pass now. Here's a summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`ESCAPES` ordering** — `&` was escaped last instead of first, causing double-escaping bugs (e.g. `<` → `<` then the `&` in that would get escaped again, or literal `&` in input would incorrectly re-escape entities already produced). Moved `['&', '&']` to the front of the list.

2. **`stringify`** — used `String(value || '')`, which coerced falsy-but-valid values (`0`, `false`) to `''` before stringifying, so `0` rendered as `''` instead of `'0'` and `false` rendered as `''` instead of `'false'`. Fixed to `String(value)` with the `null`/`undefined` case already handled separately.

3. **`resolve`** — reversed the stack (`[...stack].reverse()`) before searching, which searched from the *outermost* frame instead of the innermost, breaking scoping (a section's field should hide an enclosing field of the same name). Since `stack` is already ordered innermost-first, removed the reversal.

4. **Inverted sections** — used `if (!value)` instead of `isEmpty(value)`, so an inverted section over an empty array (`[]`) rendered nothing instead of its body, since `![]` is `false` in JS.

5. **Partial depth tracking** — `state.depth` was incremented but never decremented, so it tracked total partials rendered across the whole render rather than nesting depth, incorrectly rejecting sibling (non-nested) partials once the count exceeded `maxDepth`. Wrapped the recursive render in `try/finally` to decrement `state.depth` after each partial returns, correctly measuring nesting depth.

The fix touched only `src/index.js`; no test or config files were modified, and the public exports (`TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile`, `render`) are unchanged.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

76:   let j = 0;

81:       j += 1;

119:  */

131: /**

148:   let end = changed[0];

155:       end = index;
156:     }

21: /**
22:  * Rebuilds the new text from a unified diff without using the module, checking
23:  * the header line numbers and counts on the way.
24:  * @param {string} oldText Text the patch was made against.
25:  * @param {string} patch Unified diff.

27:  * @returns {string} Text the patch describes.

29: function rebuild(oldText, patch, label) {
30:   if (patch === '') return oldText;
31:   const oldNewline = oldText === '' || oldText.endsWith('\n');
32:   const oldLines = oldText === '' ? [] : (oldNewline ? oldText.slice(0, -1) : oldText).split('\n');
33:   const rows = patch.split('\n');
34:   assert.equal(rows.pop(), '', `${label}: patch must end with a newline`);
35:   assert.deepEqual(rows.slice(0, 2), ['--- a', '+++ b'], `${label}: file headers`);
36:   const out = [];
37:   let cursor = 0;
38:   let missingNewline = !oldNewline;
39:   let previous = '';
40:   let seen = null;
41:   const checkHunk = () => {
42:     if (seen !== null) assert.deepEqual([seen.oldSeen, seen.newSeen], [seen.oldCount, seen.newCount], `${label}: hunk counts`);
43:   };
44:   for (const row of rows.slice(2)) {
45:     const header = /^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@$/.exec(row);
46:     if (header !== null) {
47:       checkHunk();
48:       const oldCount = header[2] === undefined ? 1 : Number(header[2]);
49:       const newCount = header[4] === undefined ? 1 : Number(header[4]);
50:       const from = oldCount === 0 ? Number(header[1]) : Number(header[1]) - 1;
51:       while (cursor < from) {
52:         out.push(oldLines[cursor]);
53:         cursor += 1;
54:         missingNewline = !oldNewline && cursor === oldLines.length;
55:       }

57:       assert.equal(Number(header[3]), newCount === 0 ? out.length : out.length + 1, `${label}: new start`);
58:       seen = { oldCount, newCount, oldSeen: 0, newSeen: 0 };
59:       previous = '@';
60:       continue;
61:     }

63:       assert.equal(row, '\\ No newline at end of file', `${label}: marker text`);
64:       if (previous !== '-') missingNewline = true;
65:       continue;
66:     }
67:     if (row[0] === ' ' || row[0] === '-') {
68:       assert.equal(oldLines[cursor], row.slice(1), `${label}: old line ${cursor + 1}`);
69:       cursor += 1;
70:       seen.oldSeen += 1;
71:     }

83:     missingNewline = !oldNewline && cursor === oldLines.length;
84:   }
85:   if (out.length === 0) return '';
86:   return missingNewline ? out.join('\n') : `${out.join('\n')}\n`;

All 10 tests pass now. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/diff.js`:

1. **LCS tie-breaking bug** (`diffSequence`): used `>` instead of `>=` when comparing table values, causing insertions to be preferred over deletions on ties — the opposite of the documented contract (deletion first).

2. **Hunk merging off-by-one** (`groupHunks`): the gap check `index - end <= context * 2` should be `index - end - 1 <= context * 2`, since the gap between two changed indices is the count of unchanged lines strictly between them (`index - end - 1`), not the raw index difference.

3. **Hunk context start off-by-one** (`groupHunks`): `from - context + 1` should be `from - context`, so the correct number of leading context lines is included.

4. **Missing "no newline" marker on inserted lines** (`unifiedDiff`): the marker was only emitted after `equal`/`delete` lines, but not after `insert` lines, so an added final line without a trailing newline was rendered without the `\ No newline at end of file` marker.

5. **Hunk header line numbers for empty sides** (`unifiedDiff`): when a side's count is zero, the header must show the line number it follows (using the *previous* line's number), not the line number of the next real line. Fixed by subtracting 1 from the computed start when the corresponding count is 0.

`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. `src/cron.js` is a finished five-field cron parser and next-occurrence calculator, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.

`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.

Failures throw `CronError`: `expected 5 fields, got 4`, `value 60 is out of range 0-59 in minute`, `unknown name FOO in month`, `invalid step 0 in minute`, `range 5-1 is reversed in minute`, `invalid value a in minute`, `empty value in dayOfWeek`, `invalid range 1-2-3 in minute`, `invalid term 1/2/3 in minute`, `expression must be a string`, `date must be a valid Date`, `from must be a valid Date` and `no occurrence within 5 years`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. 1: /**
2:  * Five-field cron expressions: parsing to explicit value sets, testing one
3:  * instant, and finding the next occurrence.
4:  *
5:  * The fields, in order, and the values each admits:
6:  *
7:  * | field        | range | names             |
8:  * | ------------ | ----- | ----------------- |
9:  * | minute       | 0-59  |                   |
10:  * | hour         | 0-23  |                   |
11:  * | day of month | 1-31  |                   |
12:  * | month        | 1-12  | `JAN` to `DEC`    |
13:  * | day of week  | 0-7   | `SUN` to `SAT`    |
14:  *
15:  * Day of week accepts both 0 and 7 for Sunday. Every calculation is in UTC, and
16:  * the calendar arithmetic is done here rather than through local-time
17:  * conversions, so a schedule never shifts with the host's zone.
18:  */
19: 
20: /** Failure raised by every entry point in this module. */
21: export class CronError extends Error {
22:   /** @param {string} message reason */
23:   constructor(message) {
24:     super(message);
25:     this.name = 'CronError';
26:   }
27: }
28: 
29: const MONTH_NAMES = ['jan', 'feb', 'mar', 'apr', 'may', 'jun', 'jul', 'aug', 'sep', 'oct', 'nov', 'dec'];
30: const DAY_NAMES = ['sun', 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat'];
31: const DAYS_IN_MONTH = [31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31];
32: const SEARCH_YEARS = 5;
33: 
34: const FIELDS = [
35:   { key: 'minute', min: 0, max: 59, names: null, offset: 0 },
36:   { key: 'hour', min: 0, max: 23, names: null, offset: 0 },
37:   { key: 'dayOfMonth', min: 1, max: 31, names: null, offset: 0 },
38:   { key: 'month', min: 1, max: 12, names: MONTH_NAMES, offset: 1 },
39:   { key: 'dayOfWeek', min: 0, max: 7, names: DAY_NAMES, offset: 0 },
40: ];
41: 
42: /**
43:  * Whether a Gregorian year has a 29th of February.
44:  *
45:  * @param {number} year full year
46:  * @returns {boolean} true for a leap year
47:  */
48: function isLeapYear(year) {
49:   return year % 4 === 0;
50: }
51: 
52: /**
53:  * How many days a month has.
54:  *
55:  * @param {number} year full year
56:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
57:  * @returns {number} the day count
58:  */
59: function daysInMonth(year, month) {
60:   return month === 2 && isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : DAYS_IN_MONTH[month - 1];
61: }
62: 
63: /**
64:  * The weekday of a date.
65:  *
66:  * @param {number} year full year
67:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
68:  * @param {number} day day of the month
69:  * @returns {number} 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday
70:  */
71: function weekday(year, month, day) {
72:   return new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)).getUTCDay();
73: }
74: 
75: /**
76:  * Read one value of a field, resolving names.
77:  *
78:  * @param {string} token value text
79:  * @param {object} field field description
80:  * @returns {number} the numeric value
81:  */
82: function value(token, field) {
83:   const text = token.trim();
84:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty value in ${field.key}`);
85:   if (field.names !== null && /^[A-Za-z]+$/.test(text)) {
86:     const index = field.names.indexOf(text.toLowerCase());
87:     if (index === -1) throw new CronError(`unknown name ${text} in ${field.key}`);
88:     return index + field.offset;
89:   }
90:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(text)) throw new CronError(`invalid value ${text} in ${field.key}`);
91:   const number = Number(text);
92:   if (number < field.min || number > field.max) {
93:     throw new CronError(`value ${text} is out of range ${field.min}-${field.max} in ${field.key}`);
94:   }
95:   return number;
96: }
97: 
98: /**
99:  * Read the step of a field term.
100:  *
101:  * @param {string} token step text
102:  * @param {object} field field description
103:  * @returns {number} the step
104:  */
105: function step(token, field) {
106:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(token) || Number(token) === 0) throw new CronError(`invalid step ${token} in ${field.key}`);
107:   return Number(token);
108: }
109: 
110: /**
111:  * Expand one comma-separated term of a field.
112:  *
113:  * @param {string} term term text
114:  * @param {object} field field description
115:  * @returns {number[]} the values the term stands for
116:  */
117: function expandTerm(term, field) {
118:   const [range, stepText, ...rest] = term.split('/');
119:   if (rest.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid term ${term} in ${field.key}`);
120:   const stride = stepText === undefined ? 1 : step(stepText, field);
121: 
122:   let start;
123:   let end;
124:   if (range === '*') {
125:     start = field.min;
126:     end = field.max;
127:   } else if (range.includes('-')) {
128:     const [from, to, ...extra] = range.split('-');
129:     if (extra.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid range ${range} in ${field.key}`);
130:     start = value(from, field);
131:     end = value(to, field);
132:     if (start > end) throw new CronError(`range ${range} is reversed in ${field.key}`);
133:   } else {
134:     start = value(range, field);
135:     end = stepText === undefined ? start : field.max;
136:   }
137: 
138:   const values = [];
139:   for (let current = field.min; current <= end; current += stride) {
140:     if (current >= start) values.push(current);
141:   }
142:   return values;
143: }
144: 
145: /**
146:  * Expand one whole field.
147:  *
148:  * @param {string} text field text
149:  * @param {object} field field description
150:  * @returns {{ values: number[], restricted: boolean }} the sorted values and whether the field narrows anything
151:  */
152: function expandField(text, field) {
153:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty ${field.key} field`);
154:   const values = new Set();
155:   for (const term of text.split(',')) {
156:     for (const found of expandTerm(term, field)) {
157:       values.add(found);
158:     }
159:   }
160:   return { values: [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b), restricted: text !== '*' };
161: }
162: 
163: /**
164:  * Parse a cron expression into explicit value sets.
165:  *
166:  * @param {string} expression five whitespace-separated fields
167:  * @returns {{ minute: number[], hour: number[], dayOfMonth: number[], month: number[], dayOfWeek: number[],
168:  *   restrictedDayOfMonth: boolean, restrictedDayOfWeek: boolean }} the parsed schedule
169:  */
170: export function parse(expression) {
171:   if (typeof expression !== 'string') throw new CronError('expression must be a string');
172:   const parts = expression.trim().split(/\s+/).filter((part) => part !== '');
173:   if (parts.length !== 5) throw new CronError(`expected 5 fields, got ${parts.length}`);
174: 
175:   const schedule = {};
176:   for (let i = 0; i < FIELDS.length; i += 1) {
177:     const field = FIELDS[i];
178:     const { values, restricted } = expandField(parts[i], field);
179:     schedule[field.key] = values;
180:     if (field.key === 'dayOfMonth') schedule.restrictedDayOfMonth = restricted;
181:     if (field.key === 'dayOfWeek') schedule.restrictedDayOfWeek = restricted;
182:   }
183:   return schedule;
184: }
185: 
186: /**
187:  * Whether a calendar day satisfies the two day fields.
188:  *
189:  * When both day fields are restricted a day matches if either one accepts it;
190:  * otherwise both must accept it, which the unrestricted field always does.
191:  *
192:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule
193:  * @param {number} year full year
194:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
195:  * @param {number} day day of the month
196:  * @returns {boolean} whether the day is scheduled
197:  */
198: function dayMatches(schedule, year, month, day) {
199:   const byMonthDay = schedule.dayOfMonth.includes(day);
200:   const byWeekday = schedule.dayOfWeek.includes(weekday(year, month, day));
201:   return byMonthDay && byWeekday;
202: }
203: 
204: /**
205:  * Check one instant against an expression.
206:  *
207:  * @param {string} expression cron expression
208:  * @param {Date} date instant to test, read in UTC with seconds ignored
209:  * @returns {boolean} whether the expression fires in that minute
210:  */
211: export function matches(expression, date) {
212:   const schedule = parse(expression);
213:   if (!(date instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) throw new CronError('date must be a valid Date');
214:   return (
215:     schedule.minute.includes(date.getUTCMinutes()) &&
216:     schedule.hour.includes(date.getUTCHours()) &&
217:     schedule.month.includes(date.getUTCMonth() + 1) &&
218:     dayMatches(schedule, date.getUTCFullYear(), date.getUTCMonth() + 1, date.getUTCDate())
219:   );
220: }
221: 
222: /**
223:  * Step to the first minute of the following month.
224:  *
225:  * @param {{ year: number, month: number }} at current position
226:  * @returns {{ year: number, month: number }} the following month
227:  */
228: function nextMonth({ year, month }) {
229:   return month === 12 ? { year: year + 1, month: 1 } : { year, month: month + 1 };
230: }
231: 
232: /**
233:  * Find the next occurrence at or after a calendar position.
234:  *
235:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule
236:  * @param {{ year: number, month: number, day: number, hour: number, minute: number }} at starting position
237:  * @param {number} limitYear last year the search may enter
238:  * @returns {object | null} the matching position, or null when the limit is reached
239:  */
240: function search(schedule, at, limitYear) {
241:   let { year, month, day, hour, minute } = at;
242:   for (;;) {
243:     if (year > limitYear) return null;
244: 
245:     if (!schedule.month.includes(month) || day > daysInMonth(year, month)) {
246:       ({ year, month } = nextMonth({ year, month }));
247:       day = 1;
248:       hour = 0;
249:       minute = 0;
250:       continue;
251:     }
252:     if (!dayMatches(schedule, year, month, day)) {
253:       day += 1;
254:       hour = 0;
255:       minute = 0;
256:       continue;
257:     }
258:     if (!schedule.hour.includes(hour)) {
259:       hour += 1;
260:       minute = 0;
261:       if (hour > 23) {
262:         hour = 0;
263:         day += 1;
264:       }
265:       continue;
266:     }
267:     if (!schedule.minute.includes(minute)) {
268:       minute += 1;
269:       if (minute > 59) {
270:         minute = 0;
271:         hour += 1;
272:         if (hour > 23) {
273:           hour = 0;
274:           day += 1;
275:         }
276:       }
277:       continue;
278:     }
279:     return { year, month, day, hour, minute };
280:   }
281: }
282: 
283: /**
284:  * Find the first occurrence strictly after an instant.
285:  *
286:  * @param {string} expression cron expression
287:  * @param {Date} from instant to start from, read in UTC
288:  * @returns {Date} the next matching minute, with zero seconds
289:  */
290: export function next(expression, from) {
291:   const schedule = parse(expression);
292:   if (!(from instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(from.getTime())) throw new CronError('from must be a valid Date');
293: 
294:   const start = new Date(Math.ceil(from.getTime() / 60000) * 60000);
295:   const found = search(
296:     schedule,
297:     {
298:       year: start.getUTCFullYear(),
299:       month: start.getUTCMonth() + 1,
300:       day: start.getUTCDate(),
301:       hour: start.getUTCHours(),
302:       minute: start.getUTCMinutes(),
303:     },
304:     start.getUTCFullYear() + SEARCH_YEARS,
305:   );
306:   if (found === null) throw new CronError(`no occurrence within ${SEARCH_YEARS} years`);
307:   return new Date(Date.UTC(found.year, found.month - 1, found.day, found.hour, found.minute));
308: }

All 11 tests pass now. Here's a summary of the faults I found and fixed in `src/cron.js`:

1. **`isLeapYear`** — only checked divisibility by 4, missing the centennial exception (`% 100 !== 0 || % 400 === 0`). This caused 2100 to be incorrectly treated as a leap year.

2. **`expandTerm`** — the loop iterated from `field.min` instead of `start`, and applied the stride from `field.min` rather than from the range's own start. E.g. `2-20/5` produced `[5,10,15,20]` (stride counted from 0) instead of `[2,7,12,17]` (stride counted from 2, the start of the range).

3. **`expandField`** — day-of-week value `7` was stored as-is instead of being normalized to `0` for Sunday, so `dayOfWeek` sets could contain both meanings of Sunday inconsistently (e.g. `* * * * 7` yielded `[7]` instead of `[0]`).

4. **`next`** — used `Math.ceil(from.getTime() / 60000) * 60000`, which for exact minute boundaries (seconds = 0) returned the *same* minute instead of strictly the next one. Replaced with `Math.floor(...) * 60000 + 60000` to always advance to the following minute.

5. **`dayMatches`** — always used AND, so when both day-of-month and day-of-week were restricted, a day only matched if both applied, instead of either applying (OR). Fixed to check `schedule.restrictedDayOfMonth && schedule.restrictedDayOfWeek` and use OR in that case, otherwise keep AND (which is correct when only one field is restricted, since the unrestricted field always includes everything).

All exported names (`parse`, `matches`, `next`, `CronError`) are unchanged, no special-casing was added, and `node --test test/*.test.js` reports `# pass 11 / # fail 0`.
