`src/cron.js` is a finished five-field cron parser and next-occurrence calculator, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.

`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.

Failures throw `CronError`: `expected 5 fields, got 4`, `value 60 is out of range 0-59 in minute`, `unknown name FOO in month`, `invalid step 0 in minute`, `range 5-1 is reversed in minute`, `invalid value a in minute`, `empty value in dayOfWeek`, `invalid range 1-2-3 in minute`, `invalid term 1/2/3 in minute`, `expression must be a string`, `date must be a valid Date`, `from must be a valid Date` and `no occurrence within 5 years`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/limiter.js` implements a token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public class, its methods, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and earns `refillTokens` every `refillIntervalMs`. The refill is continuous, not stepped: time that does not add up to a whole interval still earns its share, and repeated small advances must earn exactly what one large advance of the same total would. A bucket never holds more than `capacity`, which is what bounds a burst, and it is created full, which is what allows the first burst. Time is read only through the injectable clock, and a clock that moves backwards earns nothing.

A request for `n` tokens succeeds when the bucket holds at least `n` — taking exactly what is left is a success, not a refusal. A refusal reports `retryAfterMs`, the whole number of milliseconds after which the same request would succeed, so a caller that waits exactly that long and retries is allowed; rounding it down is not good enough. A request larger than `capacity` can never be paid no matter how long the caller waits, and reports `retryAfterMs` as `null` rather than a wait that will not help. `remaining` is always whole tokens, rounded down. Buckets are independent per key, and a key whose bucket has been dropped by `reset` or `clear` starts again from a full bucket, however recently it was used.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. 1: /**
2:  * Token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key.
3:  *
4:  * A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and gains `refillTokens` every
5:  * `refillIntervalMs`, spread evenly over that interval rather than granted in
6:  * lumps, so time that does not add up to a whole interval is still credited.
7:  * Buckets are created full, which is what allows an initial burst, and time
8:  * comes from an injectable clock so callers can drive it exactly.
9:  */
10: export class RateLimiter {
11:   /** @type {Map<string, {tokens: number, updatedAt: number}>} */
12:   #buckets = new Map();
13:   #capacity;
14:   #refillTokens;
15:   #refillIntervalMs;
16:   #clock;
17:   /** @type {string | null} */
18:   #recentKey = null;
19:   /** @type {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number} | null} */
20:   #recentBucket = null;
21:   #allowed = 0;
22:   #denied = 0;
23: 
24:   /**
25:    * @param {object} options Limiter options.
26:    * @param {number} options.capacity Bucket size in tokens; a positive safe integer.
27:    * @param {number} options.refillTokens Tokens granted per interval; a positive safe integer.
28:    * @param {number} options.refillIntervalMs Length of the refill interval; a positive safe integer.
29:    * @param {() => number} [options.clock] Millisecond clock, `Date.now` by default.
30:    */
31:   constructor(options) {
32:     if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) throw new TypeError('options must be an object');
33:     const { capacity, refillTokens, refillIntervalMs, clock = Date.now } = options;
34:     checkPositiveInteger(capacity, 'capacity');
35:     checkPositiveInteger(refillTokens, 'refillTokens');
36:     checkPositiveInteger(refillIntervalMs, 'refillIntervalMs');
37:     if (typeof clock !== 'function') throw new TypeError('clock must be a function');
38:     this.#capacity = capacity;
39:     this.#refillTokens = refillTokens;
40:     this.#refillIntervalMs = refillIntervalMs;
41:     this.#clock = clock;
42:   }
43: 
44:   /** @returns {number} Bucket size in tokens. */
45:   get capacity() {
46:     return this.#capacity;
47:   }
48: 
49:   /** @returns {number} How many keys currently have a bucket. */
50:   get size() {
51:     return this.#buckets.size;
52:   }
53: 
54:   /**
55:    * Returns the bucket for a key, creating a full one when the key is new.
56:    *
57:    * The most recently used bucket is kept beside the map because callers
58:    * usually hit the same key several times in a row.
59:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
60:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The key's bucket.
61:    */
62:   #bucketFor(key) {
63:     if (this.#recentKey === key && this.#recentBucket !== null) return this.#recentBucket;
64:     let bucket = this.#buckets.get(key);
65:     if (bucket === undefined) {
66:       bucket = { tokens: this.#capacity, updatedAt: this.#clock() };
67:       this.#buckets.set(key, bucket);
68:     }
69:     this.#recentKey = key;
70:     this.#recentBucket = bucket;
71:     return bucket;
72:   }
73: 
74:   /**
75:    * Forgets the cached bucket.
76:    * @returns {void}
77:    */
78:   #forgetRecent() {
79:     this.#recentKey = null;
80:     this.#recentBucket = null;
81:   }
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * Credits the tokens earned since the bucket was last touched.
85:    *
86:    * A clock that moves backwards credits nothing and leaves the timestamp
87:    * alone, so the bucket cannot be refilled twice for the same span.
88:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Bucket to update.
89:    * @returns {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} The same bucket.
90:    */
91:   #refill(bucket) {
92:     const now = this.#clock();
93:     if (now <= bucket.updatedAt) return bucket;
94:     bucket.tokens = this.#projected(bucket, now);
95:     bucket.updatedAt = now;
96:     return bucket;
97:   }
98: 
99:   /**
100:    * Tokens a bucket would hold at a given moment, without touching it.
101:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Bucket to inspect.
102:    * @param {number} now Clock reading to project to.
103:    * @returns {number} Projected token count, never above the bucket size.
104:    */
105:   #projected(bucket, now) {
106:     const elapsed = now - bucket.updatedAt;
107:     if (elapsed <= 0) return bucket.tokens;
108:     const earned = Math.floor(elapsed / this.#refillIntervalMs) * this.#refillTokens;
109:     return Math.min(this.#capacity, bucket.tokens + earned);
110:   }
111: 
112:   /**
113:    * Milliseconds until a bucket could pay for a request.
114:    * @param {{tokens: number, updatedAt: number}} bucket Refilled bucket.
115:    * @param {number} tokens Tokens the request needs.
116:    * @returns {number | null} Zero when it can pay now, or null when the request can never be paid.
117:    */
118:   #waitFor(bucket, tokens) {
119:     if (bucket.tokens >= tokens) return 0;
120:     const deficit = tokens - bucket.tokens;
121:     return Math.floor((deficit * this.#refillIntervalMs) / this.#refillTokens);
122:   }
123: 
124:   /**
125:    * Takes tokens from a key's bucket when it can pay for them.
126:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
127:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to take; a positive safe integer.
128:    * @returns {{allowed: boolean, remaining: number, retryAfterMs: number | null}} Outcome, whole tokens left, and the wait before retrying.
129:    * @throws {TypeError} When the key or token count is malformed.
130:    */
131:   tryConsume(key, tokens = 1) {
132:     checkKey(key);
133:     checkPositiveInteger(tokens, 'tokens');
134:     const bucket = this.#refill(this.#bucketFor(key));
135:     if (bucket.tokens > tokens) {
136:       bucket.tokens -= tokens;
137:       this.#allowed += 1;
138:       return { allowed: true, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.tokens), retryAfterMs: 0 };
139:     }
140:     this.#denied += 1;
141:     return { allowed: false, remaining: Math.floor(bucket.tokens), retryAfterMs: this.#waitFor(bucket, tokens) };
142:   }
143: 
144:   /**
145:    * Takes tokens or reports the refusal as an error.
146:    * @param {string} key Bucket key.
147:    * @param {number} [tokens] Tokens to take.
148:    * @returns {number} Whole tokens left after the call.
149:    * @throws {Error} When the bucket cannot pay; the error carries `retryAfterMs`.
150:    */
151:   consume(key, tokens = 1) {
152:     const outcome = this.tryConsume(key, tokens);
153:     if (!outcome.allowed) {
154:       const error = new Error(`rate limit exceeded for "${key}"`);
155:       error.retryAfterMs = outcome.retryAfterMs;
156:       throw error;
157:     }
158:     return outcome.remaining;
159:   }
160: 
161:   /**
162:    * Takes the same number of tokens from several buckets at once, or from none
163:    * of them, so a request limited along more than one dimension cannot spend
164:    * half its budget and then be refused.

Let me rewrite the file using an integer "scaled" internal representation (tokens × refillIntervalMs) to get exact continuous refill without floating-point drift.

All 13 tests pass. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/limiter.js`:

1. **Success threshold off-by-one**: `tryConsume` used `bucket.tokens > tokens` instead of `>=`, so taking exactly what was left was wrongly refused.
2. **Requests larger than capacity weren't rejected with `null`**: `#waitFor` computed a (meaningless) wait time even when `tokens > capacity`, instead of returning `null` for a request that can never be paid.
3. **`retryAfterMs` rounded down instead of up**: `#waitFor` used `Math.floor` on the deficit-to-time conversion, which could report a wait slightly too short for the bucket to actually have refilled enough. Changed to `Math.ceil`.
4. **Refill was stepped, not continuous**: `#projected` did `Math.floor(elapsed / refillIntervalMs) * refillTokens`, discarding partial-interval progress and failing the "repeated small advances must equal one large advance" requirement. Fixed by switching to an internal integer representation scaled by `refillIntervalMs` (tracking tokens × ms), so refill/consumption arithmetic is exact and elapsed time always contributes proportionally, with no floating-point drift.
5. Updated all dependent methods (`tryConsume`, `tryConsumeAll`, `refund`, `remaining`, `waitFor`, `snapshot`, `sweep`) to work with the new scaled representation while preserving their documented contracts.
6. Also cleared the recent-bucket cache in `reset` when it drops the currently cached key, preventing a stale cached bucket from being reused after reset (this was latent but is now correctly handled).

The full random-model differential test (3000 steps checking exact integer equivalence with a reference model) now passes, confirming the continuous-refill and exact-timing behavior matches the intended contract.

goal.objective:
`src/limiter.js` implements a token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per key, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public class, its methods, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and earns `refillTokens` every `refillIntervalMs`. The refill is continuous, not stepped: time that does not add up to a whole interval still earns its share, and repeated small advances must earn exactly what one large advance of the same total would. A bucket never holds more than `capacity`, which is what bounds a burst, and it is created full, which is what allows the first burst. Time is read only through the injectable clock, and a clock that moves backwards earns nothing.

A request for `n` tokens succeeds when the bucket holds at least `n` — taking exactly what is left is a success, not a refusal. A refusal reports `retryAfterMs`, the whole number of milliseconds after which the same request would succeed, so a caller that waits exactly that long and retries is allowed; rounding it down is not good enough. A request larger than `capacity` can never be paid no matter how long the caller waits, and reports `retryAfterMs` as `null` rather than a wait that will not help. `remaining` is always whole tokens, rounded down. Buckets are independent per key, and a key whose bucket has been dropped by `reset` or `clear` starts again from a full bucket, however recently it was used.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/cron.js` is a finished five-field cron parser and next-occurrence calculator, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.

`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.

Failures throw `CronError`: `expected 5 fields, got 4`, `value 60 is out of range 0-59 in minute`, `unknown name FOO in month`, `invalid step 0 in minute`, `range 5-1 is reversed in minute`, `invalid value a in minute`, `empty value in dayOfWeek`, `invalid range 1-2-3 in minute`, `invalid term 1/2/3 in minute`, `expression must be a string`, `date must be a valid Date`, `from must be a valid Date` and `no occurrence within 5 years`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * Five-field cron expressions: parsing to explicit value sets, testing one
3:  * instant, and finding the next occurrence.
4:  *
5:  * The fields, in order, and the values each admits:
6:  *
7:  * | field        | range | names             |
8:  * | ------------ | ----- | ----------------- |
9:  * | minute       | 0-59  |                   |
10:  * | hour         | 0-23  |                   |
11:  * | day of month | 1-31  |                   |
12:  * | month        | 1-12  | `JAN` to `DEC`    |
13:  * | day of week  | 0-7   | `SUN` to `SAT`    |
14:  *
15:  * Day of week accepts both 0 and 7 for Sunday. Every calculation is in UTC, and
16:  * the calendar arithmetic is done here rather than through local-time
17:  * conversions, so a schedule never shifts with the host's zone.
18:  */

20: /** Failure raised by every entry point in this module. */
21: export class CronError extends Error {
22:   /** @param {string} message reason */
23:   constructor(message) {
24:     super(message);
25:     this.name = 'CronError';
26:   }
27: }

29: const MONTH_NAMES = ['jan', 'feb', 'mar', 'apr', 'may', 'jun', 'jul', 'aug', 'sep', 'oct', 'nov', 'dec'];
30: const DAY_NAMES = ['sun', 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat'];
31: const DAYS_IN_MONTH = [31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31];
32: const SEARCH_YEARS = 5;

34: const FIELDS = [
35:   { key: 'minute', min: 0, max: 59, names: null, offset: 0 },
36:   { key: 'hour', min: 0, max: 23, names: null, offset: 0 },
37:   { key: 'dayOfMonth', min: 1, max: 31, names: null, offset: 0 },
38:   { key: 'month', min: 1, max: 12, names: MONTH_NAMES, offset: 1 },
39:   { key: 'dayOfWeek', min: 0, max: 7, names: DAY_NAMES, offset: 0 },
40: ];

42: /**
43:  * Whether a Gregorian year has a 29th of February.
44:  *
45:  * @param {number} year full year
46:  * @returns {boolean} true for a leap year
47:  */
48: function isLeapYear(year) {
49:   return year % 4 === 0;
50: }
51: 
52: /**
53:  * How many days a month has.
54:  *
55:  * @param {number} year full year
56:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
57:  * @returns {number} the day count
58:  */
59: function daysInMonth(year, month) {
60:   return month === 2 && isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : DAYS_IN_MONTH[month - 1];
61: }
62: 
63: /**
64:  * The weekday of a date.
65:  *
66:  * @param {number} year full year
67:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
68:  * @param {number} day day of the month
69:  * @returns {number} 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday
70:  */
71: function weekday(year, month, day) {
72:   return new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)).getUTCDay();
73: }

75: /**
76:  * Read one value of a field, resolving names.
77:  *
78:  * @param {string} token value text
79:  * @param {object} field field description
80:  * @returns {number} the numeric value
81:  */
82: function value(token, field) {
83:   const text = token.trim();
84:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty value in ${field.key}`);
85:   if (field.names !== null && /^[A-Za-z]+$/.test(text)) {
86:     const index = field.names.indexOf(text.toLowerCase());
87:     if (index === -1) throw new CronError(`unknown name ${text} in ${field.key}`);
88:     return index + field.offset;
89:   }
90:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(text)) throw new CronError(`invalid value ${text} in ${field.key}`);
91:   const number = Number(text);
92:   if (number < field.min || number > field.max) {
93:     throw new CronError(`value ${text} is out of range ${field.min}-${field.max} in ${field.key}`);
94:   }
95:   return number;
96: }

98: /**
99:  * Read the step of a field term.
100:  *
101:  * @param {string} token step text
102:  * @param {object} field field description
103:  * @returns {number} the step
104:  */
105: function step(token, field) {
106:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(token) || Number(token) === 0) throw new CronError(`invalid step ${token} in ${field.key}`);
107:   return Number(token);
108: }

110: /**
111:  * Expand one comma-separated term of a field.
112:  *
113:  * @param {string} term term text
114:  * @param {object} field field description
115:  * @returns {number[]} the values the term stands for
116:  */
117: function expandTerm(term, field) {
118:   const [range, stepText, ...rest] = term.split('/');
119:   if (rest.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid term ${term} in ${field.key}`);
120:   const stride = stepText === undefined ? 1 : step(stepText, field);
121: 
122:   let start;
123:   let end;
124:   if (range === '*') {
125:     start = field.min;
126:     end = field.max;
127:   } else if (range.includes('-')) {
128:     const [from, to, ...extra] = range.split('-');
129:     if (extra.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid range ${range} in ${field.key}`);
130:     start = value(from, field);
131:     end = value(to, field);
132:     if (start > end) throw new CronError(`range ${range} is reversed in ${field.key}`);
133:   } else {
134:     start = value(range, field);
135:     end = stepText === undefined ? start : field.max;
136:   }
137: 
138:   const values = [];
139:   for (let current = field.min; current <= end; current += stride) {
140:     if (current >= start) values.push(current);
141:   }
142:   return values;
143: }
144: 
145: /**
146:  * Expand one whole field.
147:  *
148:  * @param {string} text field text
149:  * @param {object} field field description
150:  * @returns {{ values: number[], restricted: boolean }} the sorted values and whether the field narrows anything
151:  */
152: function expandField(text, field) {
153:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty ${field.key} field`);
154:   const values = new Set();
155:   for (const term of text.split(',')) {
156:     for (const found of expandTerm(term, field)) {
157:       values.add(found);
158:     }
159:   }
160:   return { values: [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b), restricted: text !== '*' };
161: }

163: /**
164:  * Parse a cron expression into explicit value sets.
165:  *
166:  * @param {string} expression five whitespace-separated fields
167:  * @returns {{ minute: number[], hour: number[], dayOfMonth: number[], month: number[], dayOfWeek: number[],
168:  *   restrictedDayOfMonth: boolean, restrictedDayOfWeek: boolean }} the parsed schedule
169:  */
170: export function parse(expression) {
171:   if (typeof expression !== 'string') throw new CronError('expression must be a string');
172:   const parts = expression.trim().split(/\s+/).filter((part) => part !== '');
173:   if (parts.length !== 5) throw new CronError(`expected 5 fields, got ${parts.length}`);
174: 
175:   const schedule = {};
176:   for (let i = 0; i < FIELDS.length; i += 1) {
177:     const field = FIELDS[i];
178:     const { values, restricted } = expandField(parts[i], field);
179:     schedule[field.key] = values;
180:     if (field.key === 'dayOfMonth') schedule.restrictedDayOfMonth = restricted;
181:     if (field.key === 'dayOfWeek') schedule.restrictedDayOfWeek = restricted;
182:   }
183:   return schedule;
184: }

186: /**
187:  * Whether a calendar day satisfies the two day fields.
188:  *
189:  * When both day fields are restricted a day matches if either one accepts it;
190:  * otherwise both must accept it, which the unrestricted field always does.
191:  *
192:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule
193:  * @param {number} year full year
194:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
195:  * @param {number} day day of the month
196:  * @returns {boolean} whether the day is scheduled
197:  */
198: function dayMatches(schedule, year, month, day) {
199:   const byMonthDay = schedule.dayOfMonth.includes(day);
200:   const byWeekday = schedule.dayOfWeek.includes(weekday(year, month, day));
201:   return byMonthDay && byWeekday;
202: }
203: 
204: /**
205:  * Check one instant against an expression.
206:  *
207:  * @param {string} expression cron expression
208:  * @param {Date} date instant to test, read in UTC with seconds ignored
209:  * @returns {boolean} whether the expression fires in that minute
210:  */
211: export function matches(expression, date) {
212:   const schedule = parse(expression);
213:   if (!(date instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) throw new CronError('date must be a valid Date');
214:   return (
215:     schedule.minute.includes(date.getUTCMinutes()) &&
216:     schedule.hour.includes(date.getUTCHours()) &&
217:     schedule.month.includes(date.getUTCMonth() + 1) &&
218:     dayMatches(schedule, date.getUTCFullYear(), date.getUTCMonth() + 1, date.getUTCDate())
219:   );
220: }

222: /**
223:  * Step to the first minute of the following month.
224:  *
225:  * @param {{ year: number, month: number }} at current position
226:  * @returns {{ year: number, month: number }} the following month
227:  */
228: function nextMonth({ year, month }) {
229:   return month === 12 ? { year: year + 1, month: 1 } : { year, month: month + 1 };
230: }

232: /**
233:  * Find the next occurrence at or after a calendar position.
234:  *
235:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule
236:  * @param {{ year: number, month: number, day: number, hour: number, minute: number }} at starting position
237:  * @param {number} limitYear last year the search may enter
238:  * @returns {object | null} the matching position, or null when the limit is reached
239:  */
240: function search(schedule, at, limitYear) {
241:   let { year, month, day, hour, minute } = at;
242:   for (;;) {
243:     if (year > limitYear) return null;
244: 
245:     if (!schedule.month.includes(month) || day > daysInMonth(year, month)) {
246:       ({ year, month } = nextMonth({ year, month }));
247:       day = 1;
248:       hour = 0;
249:       minute = 0;
250:       continue;
251:     }
252:     if (!dayMatches(schedule, year, month, day)) {
253:       day += 1;
254:       hour = 0;
255:       minute = 0;
256:       continue;
257:     }
258:     if (!schedule.hour.includes(hour)) {
259:       hour += 1;
260:       minute = 0;
261:       if (hour > 23) {
262:         hour = 0;
263:         day += 1;
264:       }
265:       continue;
266:     }
267:     if (!schedule.minute.includes(minute)) {
268:       minute += 1;
269:       if (minute > 59) {
270:         minute = 0;
271:         hour += 1;
272:         if (hour > 23) {
273:           hour = 0;
274:           day += 1;
275:         }
276:       }
277:       continue;
278:     }
279:     return { year, month, day, hour, minute };
280:   }
281: }

283: /**
284:  * Find the first occurrence strictly after an instant.
285:  *
286:  * @param {string} expression cron expression
287:  * @param {Date} from instant to start from, read in UTC
288:  * @returns {Date} the next matching minute, with zero seconds
289:  */
290: export function next(expression, from) {
291:   const schedule = parse(expression);
292:   if (!(from instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(from.getTime())) throw new CronError('from must be a valid Date');
293: 
294:   const start = new Date(Math.ceil(from.getTime() / 60000) * 60000);
295:   const found = search(
296:     schedule,
297:     {
298:       year: start.getUTCFullYear(),
299:       month: start.getUTCMonth() + 1,
300:       day: start.getUTCDate(),
301:       hour: start.getUTCHours(),
302:       minute: start.getUTCMinutes(),
303:     },
304:     start.getUTCFullYear() + SEARCH_YEARS,
305:   );
306:   if (found === null) throw new CronError(`no occurrence within ${SEARCH_YEARS} years`);
307:   return new Date(Date.UTC(found.year, found.month - 1, found.day, found.hour, found.minute));

All 11 tests pass now. Summary of the faults found and fixed in `src/cron.js`:

1. **`isLeapYear`** — only checked `year % 4 === 0`, missing the century exception. Fixed to the proper Gregorian rule: divisible by 4 and (not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400).

2. **`expandTerm`** — the loop iterated `current` from `field.min` (not from `start`) and only pushed values `>= start`, which made the *step* count from the field's minimum instead of from the start of the range (e.g. `2-20/5` produced `[5,10,15,20]` instead of `[2,7,12,17]`). Also, day-of-week values of `7` were never folded down to `0`, so `* * * * 7` yielded `[7]` instead of `[0]`, and a bare `*` on dayOfWeek included `7` giving it 8 elements instead of 7. Fixed by iterating from `start`, and normalizing `dayOfWeek` value `7` to `0` as each value is generated (which also fixes the bare-`*` dayOfWeek case since it hits the same normalization).

3. **`dayMatches`** — always ANDed the day-of-month and day-of-week results, even when both fields were restricted, where the spec (and tests) require an OR in that case. Fixed to OR when both `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek` are true, otherwise AND (which is a no-op against an unrestricted field's full set).

4. **`next`** — rounded `from` to the *nearest* future minute boundary via `Math.ceil`, which meant a `from` that already landed exactly on a minute boundary (e.g. `:00.000`) resolved to that same minute rather than strictly after it, causing `next` to return a time not strictly greater than `from`. Fixed to always advance to the start of the *following* minute: `Math.floor(from.getTime() / 60000) * 60000 + 60000`.

No behavior pinned by already-passing tests was changed, no exported names changed, and no dependencies/node_modules were introduced. Only `src/cron.js` was modified.

goal.objective:
`src/cron.js` is a finished five-field cron parser and next-occurrence calculator, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.

`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.

Failures throw `CronError`: `expected 5 fields, got 4`, `value 60 is out of range 0-59 in minute`, `unknown name FOO in month`, `invalid step 0 in minute`, `range 5-1 is reversed in minute`, `invalid value a in minute`, `empty value in dayOfWeek`, `invalid range 1-2-3 in minute`, `invalid term 1/2/3 in minute`, `expression must be a string`, `date must be a valid Date`, `from must be a valid Date` and `no occurrence within 5 years`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/index.js` holds a complete shell-like word splitter, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments` and `splitCommands`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate words. A `#` begins a comment that runs to the end of the line, but only where a word has not already started, so `a # b` yields one word and `a#b` yields one word containing the hash. Single quotes take everything literally up to the next single quote. Double quotes preserve separators, expand variables, and treat a backslash as an escape only before `$`, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash or a newline; before anything else the backslash stays in the text. Outside quotes a backslash escapes whatever follows it, and a backslash before a newline is a line continuation that disappears in both contexts. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` expand from `options.env`, where a name starts with a letter or underscore and continues with letters, digits and underscores; an unset name expands to nothing, or throws `'UNSET_VARIABLE'` when `options.strict` is set. A `$` that is followed by neither `{` nor the start of a name is an ordinary dollar character. An expanded value is inserted as it is and never split again. A word that has started produces a token even when it is empty, so `a "" b` yields three words.

Input that cannot be read throws `ShellWordsError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending character: `'UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE'` and `'UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE'` point at the opening quote, `'DANGLING_ESCAPE'` at the final backslash, and `'UNTERMINATED_BRACE'` and `'BAD_NAME'` at the `$` that started the expansion. `tokenizeDetailed` returns each word as `{ value, start, end, quoted }`, where the span covers the source text of that word and `quoted` says whether any part of it was inside quotes, one word at a time. `quote` renders a word so that reading it back yields the original: an empty word becomes a pair of single quotes, a word of only safe characters is returned unchanged, and anything else is single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped. `join` quotes each word and joins them with spaces. `parseAssignments` takes the leading run of `NAME=value` words as an environment prefix and returns the rest as the command, so an assignment-looking word after the first ordinary word stays in the command. `splitCommands` tokenizes a line and cuts it into commands at every word whose source text is a bare semicolon, so a quoted or escaped semicolon is ordinary data, and empty commands are dropped. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

2:  * A shell-like word splitter: quoting, backslash escapes, comments and
3:  * `$VAR` expansion from a caller-supplied environment, plus the inverse
4:  * quoting used to rebuild a command line.
5:  */
6: 
7: /** Error raised for input the tokenizer cannot finish reading. */
8: export class ShellWordsError extends Error {
9:   /**
10:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
11:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
12:    * @param {number} index Zero-based offset of the offending character.
13:    */
14:   constructor(code, message, index) {
15:     super(message);
16:     this.name = 'ShellWordsError';
17:     this.code = code;
18:     this.index = index;
19:   }
20: }

22: const SEPARATORS = new Set([' ', '\t', '\n']);
23: const NAME_START = /[A-Za-z_]/;
24: const NAME_CHAR = /[A-Za-z0-9_]/;
25: const NAME = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/;
26: const ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES = new Set(['$', '"', '\\', '`']);
27: const SAFE_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+$/;
28: const ASSIGNMENT = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=([\s\S]*)$/;
29: 
30: /**
31:  * Split a command line into words, reporting where each one came from.
32:  *
33:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
34:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
35:  * @returns {Array<{value: string, start: number, end: number, quoted: boolean}>} Words in order.
36:  */
37: export function tokenizeDetailed(input, options = {}) {
38:   if (typeof input !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'input must be a string', 0);
39:   if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
40:     throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'options must be an object', 0);
41:   }
42:   const env = options.env ?? {};
43:   if (typeof env !== 'object' || env === null) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'env must be an object', 0);
44:   const strict = options.strict ?? false;
45: 
46:   const tokens = [];
47:   let value = '';
48:   let started = false;
49:   let quoted = false;
50:   let start = 0;
51:   let index = 0;
52: 
53:   const begin = () => {
54:     if (!started) {
55:       started = true;
56:       start = index;
57:     }
58:   };
59: 
60:   const flush = (end) => {
61:     if (!started) return;
62:     tokens.push({ value, start, end, quoted });
63:     value = '';
64:     started = false;
65:   };
66: 
67:   const lookup = (name, at) => {
68:     if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(env, name)) return String(env[name]);
69:     if (strict) throw new ShellWordsError('UNSET_VARIABLE', `unset variable: ${name}`, at);
70:     return '';
71:   };
72: 
73:   const expand = (at) => {
74:     const next = input[at + 1];
75:     if (next === '{') {
76:       const close = input.indexOf('}', at + 2);
77:       if (close === -1) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_BRACE', 'unterminated ${', at);
78:       const name = input.slice(at + 2, close);
79:       if (!NAME.test(name)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_NAME', `invalid variable name: ${name}`, at);
80:       return [lookup(name, at), close + 1];
81:     }
82:     if (next !== undefined && NAME_START.test(next)) {
83:       let end = at + 1;
84:       while (end < input.length && NAME_CHAR.test(input[end])) end += 1;
85:       return [lookup(input.slice(at + 1, end), at), end];
86:     }
87:     return ['', at + 2];
88:   };
89: 
90:   while (index < input.length) {
91:     const character = input[index];
92: 
93:     if (SEPARATORS.has(character)) {
94:       flush(index);
95:       index += 1;
96:       continue;
97:     }
98: 
99:     if (character === '#') {
100:       while (index < input.length && input[index] !== '\n') index += 1;
101:       continue;
102:     }
103: 
104:     if (character === '\\') {
105:       begin();
106:       const next = input[index + 1];
107:       if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);

109:       index += 2;
110:       continue;
111:     }

113:     if (character === "'") {

115:       quoted = true;
116:       const close = input.indexOf("'", index + 1);

119:       }
120:       value += input.slice(index + 1, close);
121:       index = close + 1;
122:       continue;
123:     }
124: 
125:     if (character === '"') {
126:       begin();
127:       quoted = true;
128:       const openedAt = index;
129:       index += 1;
130:       let closed = false;
131:       while (index < input.length) {
132:         const inner = input[index];
133:         if (inner === '"') {
134:           closed = true;
135:           index += 1;
136:           break;
137:         }
138:         if (inner === '\\') {
139:           const next = input[index + 1];
140:           if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);
141:           if (next === '\n') {
142:             index += 2;
143:             continue;
144:           }
145:           value += next;
146:           index += 2;
147:           continue;
148:         }
149:         if (inner === '$') {
150:           const [text, after] = expand(index);
151:           value += text;
152:           index = after;
153:           continue;
154:         }
155:         value += inner;
156:         index += 1;
157:       }
158:       if (!closed) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE', 'unterminated double quote', openedAt);
159:       continue;
160:     }
161: 
162:     if (character === '$') {
163:       begin();
164:       const [text, after] = expand(index);
165:       value += text;
166:       index = after;
167:       continue;
168:     }

170:     begin();
171:     value += character;
172:     index += 1;
173:   }

179: /**

181:  *

183:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
184:  * @returns {string[]} Words in order.
185:  */
186: export function tokenize(input, options = {}) {
187:   return tokenizeDetailed(input, options).map((token) => token.value);
188: }

190: /**

194:  * @returns {string} Quoted word.

All 14 tests pass now (14/14, 0 failures). Here's a summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`quoted` flag leaked across tokens** — `begin()` didn't reset `quoted` for new words, so a previous word's quoted status bled into the next one. Fixed by resetting `quoted = false` inside `begin()`.

2. **`#` started a comment mid-word** — the `#` handler didn't check whether a word had already started, so `a#b` was wrongly split into a comment. Fixed by only treating `#` as a comment start when `!started`.

3. **Double-quote backslash escaped everything** — inside double quotes, a backslash was unconditionally consuming the next character, but per spec only `$`, `` ` ``, `"`, `\`, and newline should be escaped; before anything else the backslash must remain literal. Fixed by checking `ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES` and re-inserting the backslash otherwise.

4. **`parseAssignments` kept matching after the first ordinary word** — it scanned every token for `NAME=value` regardless of position, so assignment-looking words after the first ordinary word were wrongly captured as environment assignments instead of staying in `argv`. Fixed by stopping assignment matching once `firstArgument` is set.

5. **A lone `$` not starting a name expanded to nothing** — `expand()` returned `['', at + 2]` for a `$` followed by a non-name character, dropping the `$`. It should be treated as an ordinary `$` character. Fixed to return `['$', at + 1]`.

All changes were confined to `src/index.js`; the public API surface (`ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments`, `splitCommands`) is unchanged, no dependencies were added, and `test/` and `package.json` were untouched.

`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. All 15 tests now pass. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`cancel(id)`** only checked `status === 'running'` to refuse cancellation, so already-cancelled/missed/blocked jobs would be wrongly re-marked as `cancelled`. Fixed to only cancel jobs that are `pending`.

2. **`#blockDependents`** did a BFS but never enqueued the jobs it just blocked, so only one level of dependents was ever blocked instead of the whole transitive chain. Fixed by pushing newly-blocked job ids onto the queue.

3. **`#dependenciesSatisfied`** treated any non-pending dependency (including `running`) as satisfied, letting dependants start before their dependency actually finished. Fixed to require dependency status `=== 'done'`.

4. **`compareJobs`** ordered by deadline before priority, contradicting the spec ("highest priority first, breaking ties by ... deadline"). Swapped the order so priority is compared first.

5. **Deadline check in `#startEligible`** used `now >= job.deadlineMs` to mark a job missed, which incorrectly missed jobs starting exactly on their deadline. Fixed to `now > job.deadlineMs` so a job starting exactly at its deadline still runs.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. 1: /**
2:  * Line diff with unified output.
3:  *
4:  * Texts are compared line by line with a longest-common-subsequence walk;
5:  * output follows the unified diff format: two file headers, then one hunk per
6:  * changed region with up to `context` unchanged lines on each side.
7:  *
8:  * A line carries whether it ended with a newline, so the last line of a file
9:  * that does not end with one never matches the same text terminated normally.
10:  */
11: 
12: /** Marker printed after a line that is the end of a file without a newline. */
13: const NO_NEWLINE = '\\ No newline at end of file';
14: 
15: /**
16:  * Splits a text into lines and reports whether it ended with a newline.
17:  * @param {string} text Text to split.
18:  * @returns {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} Lines without their terminators.
19:  * @throws {TypeError} When the text is not a string.
20:  */
21: export function splitLines(text) {
22:   if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TypeError('text must be a string');
23:   if (text === '') return { lines: [], newlineAtEnd: true };
24:   const newlineAtEnd = text.endsWith('\n');
25:   const body = newlineAtEnd ? text.slice(0, -1) : text;
26:   return { lines: body.split('\n'), newlineAtEnd };
27: }
28: 
29: /**
30:  * Turns a split text into tokens that remember their terminator.
31:  * @param {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} split Result of `splitLines`.
32:  * @returns {Array<{text: string, terminated: boolean}>} One token per line.
33:  */
34: function tokenize(split) {
35:   return split.lines.map((text, index) => ({
36:     text,
37:     terminated: index < split.lines.length - 1 || split.newlineAtEnd,
38:   }));
39: }
40: 
41: /**
42:  * Builds the suffix table of longest-common-subsequence lengths.
43:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
44:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
45:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
46:  * @returns {number[][]} Table where cell `i,j` is the LCS length of the suffixes.
47:  */
48: function lcsTable(before, after, same) {
49:   const rows = before.length;
50:   const columns = after.length;
51:   const table = Array.from({ length: rows + 1 }, () => new Array(columns + 1).fill(0));
52:   for (let i = rows - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
53:     for (let j = columns - 1; j >= 0; j -= 1) {
54:       table[i][j] = same(before[i], after[j])
55:         ? table[i + 1][j + 1] + 1
56:         : Math.max(table[i + 1][j], table[i][j + 1]);
57:     }
58:   }
59:   return table;
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Diffs two sequences.
64:  *
65:  * Where a deletion and an insertion are equally good, the deletion is emitted
66:  * first, so a replaced item reads as `-old` then `+new`.
67:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
68:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
69:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
70:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', item: unknown}>} Operations in file order.
71:  */
72: function diffSequence(before, after, same) {
73:   const table = lcsTable(before, after, same);
74:   const ops = [];
75:   let i = 0;
76:   let j = 0;
77:   while (i < before.length && j < after.length) {
78:     if (same(before[i], after[j])) {
79:       ops.push({ type: 'equal', item: before[i] });
80:       i += 1;
81:       j += 1;
82:     } else if (table[i + 1][j] > table[i][j + 1]) {
83:       ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
84:       i += 1;
85:     } else {
86:       ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
87:       j += 1;
88:     }
89:   }
90:   while (i < before.length) {
91:     ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
92:     i += 1;
93:   }
94:   while (j < after.length) {
95:     ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
96:     j += 1;
97:   }
98:   return ops;
99: }
100: 
101: /**
102:  * Diffs two line arrays, comparing line text alone.
103:  * @param {string[]} before Old lines.
104:  * @param {string[]} after New lines.
105:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', line: string}>} Operations in file order.
106:  * @throws {TypeError} When either argument is not an array of strings.
107:  */
108: export function diffLines(before, after) {
109:   checkLines(before);
110:   checkLines(after);
111:   return diffSequence(before, after, (a, b) => a === b).map((op) => ({ type: op.type, line: op.item }));
112: }

115:  * Counts added, removed, and unchanged lines between two texts.

1. **LCS tie-breaking (line 82)**: `table[i+1][j] > table[i][j+1]` should be `>=`. The contract requires that when a deletion and an insertion are equally good, the deletion is emitted first — but strict `>` was letting insertions win ties, producing `+new` before `-old` for replacements.

2. **Hunk merging threshold (`groupHunks`)**: the gap check `index - end <= context * 2` didn't account for the fact that `end` and `index` are indices of *changed* lines, so the number of unchanged lines between them is `index - end - 1`. Fixed to `index - end - 1 <= context * 2` so hunks merge exactly when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, per spec.

3. **Hunk start padding (`groupHunks`)**: `Math.max(0, from - context + 1)` was off by one, dropping one line of leading context. Fixed to `Math.max(0, from - context)`.

4. **Zero-count hunk header numbering**: when a side contributes zero lines, the header must report the line number it *follows* rather than the position of the next line. Added a check so `oldStart`/`newStart` subtract one from the position when `oldCount`/`newCount` is `0`.

5. **Missing "No newline" marker on inserted lines**: the marker was only emitted after `equal` and `delete` lines, never after `insert` lines, so a diff ending with an unterminated inserted line lost the marker. Added the same marker emission after `+` lines.

goal.objective:
`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

content.text:
`src/index.js` holds a complete shell-like word splitter, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments` and `splitCommands`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate words. A `#` begins a comment that runs to the end of the line, but only where a word has not already started, so `a # b` yields one word and `a#b` yields one word containing the hash. Single quotes take everything literally up to the next single quote. Double quotes preserve separators, expand variables, and treat a backslash as an escape only before `$`, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash or a newline; before anything else the backslash stays in the text. Outside quotes a backslash escapes whatever follows it, and a backslash before a newline is a line continuation that disappears in both contexts. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` expand from `options.env`, where a name starts with a letter or underscore and continues with letters, digits and underscores; an unset name expands to nothing, or throws `'UNSET_VARIABLE'` when `options.strict` is set. A `$` that is followed by neither `{` nor the start of a name is an ordinary dollar character. An expanded value is inserted as it is and never split again. A word that has started produces a token even when it is empty, so `a "" b` yields three words.

Input that cannot be read throws `ShellWordsError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending character: `'UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE'` and `'UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE'` point at the opening quote, `'DANGLING_ESCAPE'` at the final backslash, and `'UNTERMINATED_BRACE'` and `'BAD_NAME'` at the `$` that started the expansion. `tokenizeDetailed` returns each word as `{ value, start, end, quoted }`, where the span covers the source text of that word and `quoted` says whether any part of it was inside quotes, one word at a time. `quote` renders a word so that reading it back yields the original: an empty word becomes a pair of single quotes, a word of only safe characters is returned unchanged, and anything else is single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped. `join` quotes each word and joins them with spaces. `parseAssignments` takes the leading run of `NAME=value` words as an environment prefix and returns the rest as the command, so an assignment-looking word after the first ordinary word stays in the command. `splitCommands` tokenizes a line and cuts it into commands at every word whose source text is a bare semicolon, so a quoted or escaped semicolon is ordinary data, and empty commands are dropped. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * A shell-like word splitter: quoting, backslash escapes, comments and
3:  * `$VAR` expansion from a caller-supplied environment, plus the inverse
4:  * quoting used to rebuild a command line.
5:  */
6: 
7: /** Error raised for input the tokenizer cannot finish reading. */
8: export class ShellWordsError extends Error {
9:   /**
10:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
11:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
12:    * @param {number} index Zero-based offset of the offending character.
13:    */
14:   constructor(code, message, index) {
15:     super(message);
16:     this.name = 'ShellWordsError';
17:     this.code = code;
18:     this.index = index;
19:   }
20: }
21: 
22: const SEPARATORS = new Set([' ', '\t', '\n']);
23: const NAME_START = /[A-Za-z_]/;
24: const NAME_CHAR = /[A-Za-z0-9_]/;
25: const NAME = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/;
26: const ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES = new Set(['$', '"', '\\', '`']);
27: const SAFE_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+$/;
28: const ASSIGNMENT = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=([\s\S]*)$/;
29: 
30: /**
31:  * Split a command line into words, reporting where each one came from.
32:  *
33:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
34:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
35:  * @returns {Array<{value: string, start: number, end: number, quoted: boolean}>} Words in order.
36:  */
37: export function tokenizeDetailed(input, options = {}) {
38:   if (typeof input !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'input must be a string', 0);
39:   if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
40:     throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'options must be an object', 0);
41:   }
42:   const env = options.env ?? {};
43:   if (typeof env !== 'object' || env === null) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'env must be an object', 0);
44:   const strict = options.strict ?? false;
45: 
46:   const tokens = [];
47:   let value = '';
48:   let started = false;
49:   let quoted = false;
50:   let start = 0;
51:   let index = 0;
52: 
53:   const begin = () => {
54:     if (!started) {
55:       started = true;
56:       start = index;
57:     }
58:   };
59: 
60:   const flush = (end) => {
61:     if (!started) return;
62:     tokens.push({ value, start, end, quoted });
63:     value = '';
64:     started = false;
65:   };
66: 
67:   const lookup = (name, at) => {
68:     if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(env, name)) return String(env[name]);
69:     if (strict) throw new ShellWordsError('UNSET_VARIABLE', `unset variable: ${name}`, at);
70:     return '';
71:   };
72: 
73:   const expand = (at) => {
74:     const next = input[at + 1];
75:     if (next === '{') {
76:       const close = input.indexOf('}', at + 2);
77:       if (close === -1) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_BRACE', 'unterminated ${', at);
78:       const name = input.slice(at + 2, close);
79:       if (!NAME.test(name)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_NAME', `invalid variable name: ${name}`, at);
80:       return [lookup(name, at), close + 1];
81:     }
82:     if (next !== undefined && NAME_START.test(next)) {
83:       let end = at + 1;
84:       while (end < input.length && NAME_CHAR.test(input[end])) end += 1;
85:       return [lookup(input.slice(at + 1, end), at), end];
86:     }
87:     return ['', at + 2];
88:   };
89: 
90:   while (index < input.length) {
91:     const character = input[index];
92: 
93:     if (SEPARATORS.has(character)) {
94:       flush(index);
95:       index += 1;
96:       continue;
97:     }
98: 
99:     if (character === '#') {
100:       while (index < input.length && input[index] !== '\n') index += 1;
101:       continue;
102:     }
103: 
104:     if (character === '\\') {
105:       begin();
106:       const next = input[index + 1];
107:       if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);
108:       if (next !== '\n') value += next;
109:       index += 2;
110:       continue;
111:     }
112: 
113:     if (character === "'") {
114:       begin();
115:       quoted = true;
116:       const close = input.indexOf("'", index + 1);
117:       if (close === -1) {
118:         throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE', 'unterminated single quote', index);
119:       }
120:       value += input.slice(index + 1, close);
121:       index = close + 1;
122:       continue;
123:     }
124: 
125:     if (character === '"') {
126:       begin();
127:       quoted = true;
128:       const openedAt = index;
129:       index += 1;
130:       let closed = false;
131:       while (index < input.length) {
132:         const inner = input[index];
133:         if (inner === '"') {
134:           closed = true;
135:           index += 1;
136:           break;
137:         }
138:         if (inner === '\\') {
139:           const next = input[index + 1];
140:           if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);
141:           if (next === '\n') {
142:             index += 2;
143:             continue;
144:           }
145:           value += next;
146:           index += 2;
147:           continue;
148:         }
149:         if (inner === '$') {
150:           const [text, after] = expand(index);
151:           value += text;
152:           index = after;
153:           continue;
154:         }
155:         value += inner;
156:         index += 1;
157:       }
158:       if (!closed) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE', 'unterminated double quote', openedAt);
159:       continue;
160:     }
161: 
162:     if (character === '$') {
163:       begin();
164:       const [text, after] = expand(index);
165:       value += text;
166:       index = after;
167:       continue;
168:     }
169: 
170:     begin();
171:     value += character;
172:     index += 1;
173:   }
174: 
175:   flush(index);
176:   return tokens;
177: }
178: 
179: /**
180:  * Split a command line into words.
181:  *
182:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
183:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
184:  * @returns {string[]} Words in order.
185:  */
186: export function tokenize(input, options = {}) {
187:   return tokenizeDetailed(input, options).map((token) => token.value);
188: }
189: 
190: /**
191:  * Quote one word so a tokenizer reads it back unchanged.
192:  *
193:  * @param {string} word Word to quote.
194:  * @returns {string} Quoted word.
195:  */
196: export function quote(word) {
197:   if (typeof word !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'word must be a string', 0);
198:   if (word === '') return "''";
199:   if (SAFE_WORD.test(word)) return word;
200:   return `'${word.split("'").join("'\\''")}'`;
201: }
202: 
203: /**
204:  * Quote and join words into a command line.
205:  *
206:  * @param {string[]} words Words to join.
207:  * @returns {string} Command line.
208:  */
209: export function join(words) {
210:   if (!Array.isArray(words)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'words must be an array', 0);
211:   return words.map((word) => quote(word)).join(' ');
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Split leading `NAME=value` words from the command they precede.
216:  *
217:  * @param {string[]} tokens Words produced by the tokenizer.
218:  * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, string>, argv: string[]}} Prefix assignments and the remaining words.
219:  */
220: export function parseAssignments(tokens) {
221:   if (!Array.isArray(tokens)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'tokens must be an array', 0);
222:   const assignments = {};
223:   let firstArgument = -1;
224:   let index = 0;
225:   while (index < tokens.length) {
226:     const token = tokens[index];
227:     if (typeof token !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'tokens must be strings', index);
228:     const match = ASSIGNMENT.exec(token);
229:     if (match === null) {
230:       if (firstArgument === -1) firstArgument = index;
231:     } else {
232:       assignments[match[1]] = match[2];
233:     }
234:     index += 1;
235:   }
236:   return { assignments, argv: tokens.slice(firstArgument === -1 ? tokens.length : firstArgument) };
237: }
238: 
239: /**
240:  * Split a command line into commands separated by bare semicolons.
241:  *
242:  * A semicolon only separates when the whole word was written as a bare `;`, so
243:  * a quoted or escaped semicolon stays part of its command.
244:  *
245:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
246:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
247:  * @returns {string[][]} One word list per command, with empty commands dropped.
248:  */
249: export function splitCommands(input, options = {}) {
250:   const commands = [];
251:   let current = [];
252:   for (const token of tokenizeDetailed(input, options)) {
253:     if (input.slice(token.start, token.end) === ';') {
254:       if (current.length > 0) commands.push(current);
255:       current = [];
256:       continue;
257:     }
258:     current.push(token.value);
259:   }
260:   if (current.length > 0) commands.push(current);
261:   return commands;
262: }

5: /** Deterministic 32-bit PRNG so generated command lines replay identically. */
6: function mulberry32(seed) {
7:   let a = seed >>> 0;
8:   return function next() {
9:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
10:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
11:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
12:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
13:   };
14: }

16: test('whitespace separates words', () => {
17:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('ls -la /tmp'), ['ls', '-la', '/tmp']);
18:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('  spaced   out  '), ['spaced', 'out']);
19:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('tab\tseparated\nlines'), ['tab', 'separated', 'lines']);
20:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize(''), []);
21:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('   '), []);
22:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('one'), ['one']);
23: });
24: 
25: test('single quotes take everything literally', () => {
26:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("'a b'"), ['a b']);
27:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("'$HOME #x \\n'"), ['$HOME #x \\n']);
28:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("''"), ['']);
29:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("a''b"), ['ab']);
30:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("'a'\\''b'"), ["a'b"]);
31:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("pre'mid'post"), ['premidpost']);
32: });
33: 
34: test('double quotes keep spaces but expand variables', () => {
35:   const env = { NAME: 'bo', EMPTY: '' };
36:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a b"'), ['a b']);
37:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"hi $NAME"', { env }), ['hi bo']);
38:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"${NAME}s"', { env }), ['bos']);
39:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('""'), ['']);
40:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a"b c"d'), ['ab cd']);
41:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"$EMPTY"', { env }), ['']);
42: });

44: test('a backslash inside double quotes escapes only four characters', () => {
45:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\"b"'), ['a"b']);
46:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\\\b"'), ['a\\b']);
47:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\$b"'), ['a$b']);
48:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\`b"'), ['a`b']);
49:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\nb"'), ['a\\nb'], 'a backslash before n stays literal');
50:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\tb"'), ['a\\tb'], 'a backslash before t stays literal');
51:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"c:\\path"'), ['c:\\path']);
52:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"a\\\nb"'), ['ab'], 'a backslash before a newline continues the line');
53: });

55: test('a backslash outside quotes escapes anything', () => {
56:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a\\ b'), ['a b']);
57:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('\\$HOME'), ['$HOME']);
58:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a\\\\b'), ['a\\b']);
59:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('\\#not-a-comment'), ['#not-a-comment']);
60:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a\\\nb'), ['ab']);
61:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('\\"quoted\\"'), ['"quoted"']);
62: });

64: test('a comment needs to start a word', () => {
65:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a # b'), ['a']);
66:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a#b'), ['a#b'], 'a hash inside a word is an ordinary character');
67:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('#everything'), []);
68:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a # b\nc'), ['a', 'c']);
69:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('"#"'), ['#']);
70:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("a '#' b"), ['a', '#', 'b']);
71:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('x=1#2'), ['x=1#2']);
72:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a "b"#c'), ['a', 'b#c']);
73: });

75: test('variables expand from the given environment only', () => {
76:   const env = { FOO: 'bar', N: '3', SPACED: 'x y' };
77:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$FOO', { env }), ['bar']);
78:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('${FOO}', { env }), ['bar']);
79:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a${FOO}b', { env }), ['abarb']);
80:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$FOO$N', { env }), ['bar3']);
81:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$SPACED', { env }), ['x y'], 'an expansion is never split again');
82:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$MISSING', { env }), ['']);
83:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('a$MISSING', { env }), ['a']);
84:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize("'$FOO'", { env }), ['$FOO']);
85:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$FOO_', { env }), [''], 'the name runs to the last name character');
86: });

89:   assert.deepEqual(tokenize('$1'), ['$1']);

## Summary of defects fixed in `src/index.js`

1. **`quoted` flag leaked across tokens** — `flush()` never reset `quoted` to `false`, so once any word was quoted, every subsequent word (like `plain` in `echo "hi $NAME" plain`) was incorrectly marked `quoted: true`. Fixed by resetting `quoted = false` inside `flush`.

2. **Lone `$` handling was wrong** — `expand()` returned `['', at + 2]` for a `$` not followed by `{` or a name-start character, which both discarded the `$` and skipped an extra character. Per spec, such a `$` is just an ordinary dollar character, so it should return `['$', at + 1]`.

3. **Comment detection ignored word-start state** — the `#` branch fired unconditionally, so `a#b` was wrongly treated as `a` + comment instead of one word `a#b`. Fixed by only starting a comment when `!started`.

4. **Double-quote backslash escaping was too permissive** — the code escaped *any* character following `\` inside double quotes, but the spec only allows escaping `$`, `` ` ``, `"`, `\`, and newline; any other character should keep the backslash literally. Fixed by checking `ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES.has(next)` and otherwise emitting the backslash itself and advancing by one.

5. **`parseAssignments` kept scanning after the first ordinary word** — it continued treating later `NAME=value`-shaped tokens as assignments even after the argv boundary was found, incorrectly merging `C=3` into `assignments` in addition to leaving it in `argv`. Fixed by only evaluating tokens as assignments while `firstArgument === -1`.

All fixes were confined to `src/index.js`; the public API surface, exports, and previously-passing behavior are unchanged.

The intended behaviour is this. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate words. A `#` begins a comment that runs to the end of the line, but only where a word has not already started, so `a # b` yields one word and `a#b` yields one word containing the hash. Single quotes take everything literally up to the next single quote. Double quotes preserve separators, expand variables, and treat a backslash as an escape only before `$`, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash or a newline; before anything else the backslash stays in the text.
