A word that has started produces a token even when it is empty, so `a "" b` yields three words.

Input that cannot be read throws `ShellWordsError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending character: `'UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE'` and `'UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE'` point at the opening quote, `'DANGLING_ESCAPE'` at the final backslash, and `'UNTERMINATED_BRACE'` and `'BAD_NAME'` at the `$` that started the expansion. `tokenizeDetailed` returns each word as `{ value, start, end, quoted }`, where the span covers the source text of that word and `quoted` says whether any part of it was inside quotes, one word at a time. `quote` renders a word so that reading it back yields the original: an empty word becomes a pair of single quotes, a word of only safe characters is returned unchanged, and anything else is single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped. `join` quotes each word and joins them with spaces. `parseAssignments` takes the leading run of `NAME=value` words as an environment prefix and returns the rest as the command, so an assignment-looking word after the first ordinary word stays in the command. `splitCommands` tokenizes a line and cuts it into commands at every word whose source text is a bare semicolon, so a quoted or escaped semicolon is ordinary data, and empty commands are dropped. `src/bitset.js` holds a fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words and `src/bloom.js` builds a Bloom filter on top of it. The test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public classes, their methods, their signatures, the hash functions, and the byte layout exactly as they are — the serialized form is pinned by the tests — along with every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the modules' own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. The byte form gives byte `b` the bits `8b` through `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, so a byte carries every one of its eight bits and the whole set survives a trip through `toBytes` and `fromBytes`.

The Bloom filter derives two 32-bit hashes from a value and its seed and probes `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits` for each of its `hashes` rounds. Those hashes are 32-bit values and the arithmetic that combines them is 32-bit and unsigned: every probe must land on a valid bit index for any input. A value that was added is always reported as present. `union` merges two filters only when they agree on their bit count, their probe count, and their seed, and refuses otherwise with a `RangeError`. `serialize` writes a four-byte signature, the bit count, the seed, the probe count, the number of added values, and then the bits; `deserialize` restores all of it.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the modules by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

**`src/bitset.js`**

4. **Probe index computed with signed arithmetic** — `(first + Math.imul(index, second)) % this.#bits` could go negative/overflow signed 32-bit range before the modulo, producing invalid (negative) bit indices. Fixed by forcing unsigned with `>>> 0` before the modulo.

goal.objective:
`src/bitset.js` holds a fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words and `src/bloom.js` builds a Bloom filter on top of it. The test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public classes, their methods, their signatures, the hash functions, and the byte layout exactly as they are — the serialized form is pinned by the tests — along with every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the modules' own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. The byte form gives byte `b` the bits `8b` through `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, so a byte carries every one of its eight bits and the whole set survives a trip through `toBytes` and `fromBytes`.

The Bloom filter derives two 32-bit hashes from a value and its seed and probes `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits` for each of its `hashes` rounds. Those hashes are 32-bit values and the arithmetic that combines them is 32-bit and unsigned: every probe must land on a valid bit index for any input. A value that was added is always reported as present. `union` merges two filters only when they agree on their bit count, their probe count, and their seed, and refuses otherwise with a `RangeError`. `serialize` writes a four-byte signature, the bit count, the seed, the probe count, the number of added values, and then the bits; `deserialize` restores all of it.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the modules by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. 2:  * Fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words.
3:  *
4:  * Bits are numbered from zero. The byte form is portable: byte `b` carries
5:  * bits `8b` to `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, and any bits
6:  * past the declared size are zero.
7:  */
8: export class BitSet {
9:   #nbits;
10:   #words;
11: 
12:   /**
13:    * @param {number} nbits How many bits the set holds; a positive safe integer.
14:    * @throws {TypeError} When the size is not a positive safe integer.
15:    */
16:   constructor(nbits) {
17:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(nbits) || nbits <= 0) throw new TypeError('size must be a positive integer');
18:     this.#nbits = nbits;
19:     this.#words = new Uint32Array(Math.floor(nbits / 32));
20:   }
21: 
22:   /** @returns {number} How many bits the set holds. */
23:   get size() {
24:     return this.#nbits;
25:   }
26: 
27:   /**
28:    * Validates a bit index.
29:    * @param {unknown} index Candidate index.
30:    * @returns {number} The index itself.
31:    * @throws {RangeError} When the index is outside `0 .. size - 1`.
32:    */
33:   #check(index) {
34:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > this.#nbits) {
35:       throw new RangeError(`bit index out of range: ${String(index)}`);
36:     }
37:     return index;
38:   }
39: 
40:   /**
41:    * Turns a bit on.
42:    * @param {number} index Bit to set.
43:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
44:    */
45:   set(index) {
46:     this.#check(index);
47:     this.#words[index >>> 5] |= 1 << (index & 31);
48:     return this;
49:   }
50: 
51:   /**
52:    * Turns a bit off.
53:    * @param {number} index Bit to clear.
54:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
55:    */
56:   clear(index) {
57:     this.#check(index);
58:     this.#words[index >>> 5] &= ~(1 << (index & 31));
59:     return this;
60:   }
61: 
62:   /**
63:    * Flips a bit.
64:    * @param {number} index Bit to flip.
65:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
66:    */
67:   toggle(index) {
68:     this.#check(index);
69:     this.#words[index >>> 5] ^= 1 << (index & 31);
70:     return this;
71:   }
72: 
73:   /**
74:    * Reads a bit.
75:    * @param {number} index Bit to read.
76:    * @returns {boolean} True when the bit is on.
77:    */
78:   get(index) {
79:     this.#check(index);
80:     return (this.#words[index >>> 5] & (1 << (index & 31))) !== 0;
81:   }
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * Counts the bits that are on.
85:    * @returns {number} Population count.
86:    */
87:   count() {
88:     let total = 0;
89:     for (const word of this.#words) total += popcount(word);
90:     return total;
91:   }

93:   /**

104:     }

110:    * @returns {Uint32Array} The backing words.
111:    */
112:   words() {
113:     return this.#words;
114:   }

119:    * @returns {BitSet} New set holding every bit of either input.
120:    * @throws {RangeError} When the sizes differ.
121:    */

5:  *
6:  * Two 32-bit FNV-1a hashes are derived from the value and the seed; probe `i`

8:  * valid bit index. A filter answers `has` with no false negatives; a `true`

14: /** Bytes of header before the bit payload. */
15: const HEADER_BYTES = 17;
16: /** FNV-1a 32-bit offset basis. */
17: const FNV_OFFSET = 0x811c9dc5;
18: /** FNV-1a 32-bit prime. */

20: /** Constant mixed into the seed for the second hash. */
21: const SECOND_SEED = 0x9e3779b9;

23: /**
24:  * FNV-1a over the UTF-16 code units of a string.
25:  * @param {string} value Value to hash.
26:  * @param {number} seed Starting seed.
27:  * @returns {number} Unsigned 32-bit hash.
28:  */
29: function fnv1a(value, seed) {
30:   let hash = (FNV_OFFSET ^ seed) >>> 0;
31:   for (let index = 0; index < value.length; index += 1) {
32:     hash = (hash ^ value.charCodeAt(index)) >>> 0;
33:     hash = Math.imul(hash, FNV_PRIME) >>> 0;

1: import { test } from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
3: 
4: import { BloomFilter } from '../src/bloom.js';
5: 
6: /** Values used to exercise the probe arithmetic. */
7: const WORDS = [
8:   'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', 'delta', 'epsilon', 'zeta', 'eta', 'theta', 'iota', 'kappa',
9:   'lambda', 'mu', 'nu', 'xi', 'omicron', 'pi', 'rho', 'sigma', 'tau', 'upsilon',
10:   'key-a', 'key-b', 'key-c', 'user:1', 'user:2', 'user:3', '', '\u{1F600}', 'héllo', 'a'.repeat(64),
11: ];
12: 
13: /**
14:  * Builds a filter holding every word.
15:  * @param {object} options Filter options.
16:  * @param {string[]} [values] Values to add.
17:  * @returns {BloomFilter} Populated filter.
18:  */
19: function populated(options, values = WORDS) {
20:   const filter = new BloomFilter(options);
21:   for (const value of values) filter.add(value);
22:   return filter;
23: }
24: 
25: test('every added value is reported as present', () => {
26:   const filter = populated({ bits: 512, hashes: 4 });
27:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(filter.has(value), true, `has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
28:   assert.equal(filter.count, WORDS.length);
29:   assert.ok(filter.fillRatio() > 0 && filter.fillRatio() <= 1, `fill ratio ${filter.fillRatio()}`);
30:   const wide = populated({ bits: 4096, hashes: 7, seed: 12345 });
31:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(wide.has(value), true, `wide has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
32:   const tight = populated({ bits: 37, hashes: 3, seed: 0xffffffff });
33:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(tight.has(value), true, `tight has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
34: });
35: 
36: test('an empty filter reports nothing and misses are usually detected', () => {
37:   const empty = new BloomFilter({ bits: 1024, hashes: 5 });
38:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(empty.has(value), false, `empty has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
39:   assert.deepEqual([empty.count, empty.fillRatio()], [0, 0]);
40:   const filter = populated({ bits: 4096, hashes: 6 });
41:   const absent = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, index) => `missing-${index}`);
42:   const positives = absent.filter((value) => filter.has(value));
43:   assert.ok(positives.length < 5, `too many false positives: ${positives.length}`);
44: });
45: 
46: test('the same values and seed produce the same bits', () => {
47:   const first = populated({ bits: 256, hashes: 3, seed: 7 });
48:   const second = populated({ bits: 256, hashes: 3, seed: 7 }, [...WORDS].reverse());
49:   assert.deepEqual([...first.serialize()], [...second.serialize()]);
50:   const seeded = populated({ bits: 256, hashes: 3, seed: 8 });
51:   assert.notDeepEqual([...seeded.serialize()], [...first.serialize()]);
52:   assert.deepEqual([first.bits, first.hashes, first.seed], [256, 3, 7]);
53: });
54: 
55: test('union merges filters built the same way and refuses the rest', () => {
56:   const left = populated({ bits: 512, hashes: 4, seed: 3 }, WORDS.slice(0, 10));
57:   const right = populated({ bits: 512, hashes: 4, seed: 3 }, WORDS.slice(10, 20));
58:   const merged = left.union(right);
59:   for (const value of WORDS.slice(0, 20)) assert.equal(merged.has(value), true, `merged has ${value}`);
60:   assert.deepEqual([merged.count, merged.bits, merged.hashes, merged.seed], [20, 512, 4, 3]);
61:   assert.equal(left.count, 10);
62:   const bad = [
63:     [() => left.union(new BloomFilter({ bits: 256, hashes: 4, seed: 3 })), 'RangeError'],
64:     [() => left.union(new BloomFilter({ bits: 512, hashes: 5, seed: 3 })), 'RangeError'],
65:     [() => left.union(new BloomFilter({ bits: 512, hashes: 4, seed: 4 })), 'RangeError'],
66:   ];
67:   for (const [call, name] of bad) {
68:     assert.throws(call, { name, message: 'bloom filters must share their parameters' });
69:   }
70:   assert.throws(() => left.union({}), { name: 'TypeError', message: 'argument must be a BloomFilter' });
71: });
72: 
73: test('a serialized filter round-trips through bytes', () => {
74:   const filter = populated({ bits: 512, hashes: 4, seed: 0 });
75:   const bytes = filter.serialize();
76:   assert.deepEqual([...bytes.slice(0, 17)], [66, 76, 77, 49, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 30, 0, 0, 0]);
77:   assert.equal(bytes.length, 17 + 64);
78:   const restored = BloomFilter.deserialize(bytes);
79:   assert.deepEqual([restored.bits, restored.hashes, restored.seed, restored.count], [512, 4, 0, WORDS.length]);
80:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(restored.has(value), true, `restored has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
81:   assert.deepEqual([...restored.serialize()], [...bytes]);
82:   const odd = populated({ bits: 100, hashes: 3, seed: 9 });
83:   const oddBytes = odd.serialize();
84:   assert.equal(oddBytes.length, 17 + 13);
85:   const oddBack = BloomFilter.deserialize(oddBytes);
86:   for (const value of WORDS) assert.equal(oddBack.has(value), true, `odd restored has ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
87: });
88: 
89: test('malformed options and payloads are refused', () => {
90:   const bytes = populated({ bits: 512, hashes: 4 }).serialize();
91:   const bad = [
92:     [() => new BloomFilter(), 'TypeError', 'options must be an object'],
93:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 0, hashes: 1 }), 'TypeError', 'bits must be a positive integer'],
94:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 8, hashes: 0 }), 'TypeError', 'hashes must be a positive integer'],
95:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 8, hashes: 1, seed: -1 }), 'TypeError', 'seed must be a 32-bit unsigned integer'],
96:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 8, hashes: 1, seed: 2 ** 32 }), 'TypeError', 'seed must be a 32-bit unsigned integer'],
97:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 8, hashes: 1 }).add(7), 'TypeError', 'value must be a string'],
98:     [() => new BloomFilter({ bits: 8, hashes: 1 }).has(null), 'TypeError', 'value must be a string'],
99:     [() => BloomFilter.deserialize([...bytes]), 'TypeError', 'bytes must be a Uint8Array'],
100:     [() => BloomFilter.deserialize(new Uint8Array(4)), 'Error', 'unrecognised bloom filter header'],
101:     [() => BloomFilter.deserialize(bytes.slice(0, 40)), 'RangeError', 'serialized length does not match the header'],
102:   ];
103:   for (const [call, name, message] of bad) assert.throws(call, { name, message }, message);
104: });

**Defects found and fixed in `cell-LusByP`:**

**`src/bitset.js`** (3 bugs):
1. **Word allocation**: `Math.floor(nbits / 32)` under-allocated words for sizes not divisible by 32 (e.g., size 100 got only 3 words instead of 4). Fixed to `Math.ceil(nbits / 32)`.
2. **Off-by-one bounds check**: `#check` allowed `index === this.#nbits` (used `>` instead of `>=`), letting an out-of-range index slip through instead of being refused. Fixed to `index >= this.#nbits`.
3. **`toBytes` bit corruption**: used `bytes[index >>> 3] = 1 << (index & 7)` (assignment) instead of `|=` (OR-assignment), so each new bit in a byte overwrote the previous ones instead of accumulating. Fixed to `|=`.

**`src/bloom.js`** (2 bugs):
1. **Unsigned arithmetic in probing**: `(first + Math.imul(index, second)) % this.#bits` could go negative in JS (since `Math.imul` returns a signed 32-bit int and the sum could overflow into negative territory), producing negative probe indices that `BitSet` then rejected. Fixed by coercing to unsigned before the modulo: `((first + Math.imul(index, second)) >>> 0) % this.#bits`.
2. **`union` compatibility check incomplete**: only compared `bits`, not `hashes` or `seed`, so filters with mismatched probe counts or seeds were merged instead of being refused. Fixed to check all three: `other.bits !== this.#bits || other.hashes !== this.#hashes || other.seed !== this.#seed`.

All fixes preserve the public API, method signatures, hash functions, and byte layout exactly as specified — only correcting the underlying implementation defects. Confirmed with `node --test test/*.test.js` (13/13 passing) and `test ! -e node_modules` (no dependencies installed).

goal.objective:
`src/bitset.js` holds a fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words and `src/bloom.js` builds a Bloom filter on top of it. The test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public classes, their methods, their signatures, the hash functions, and the byte layout exactly as they are — the serialized form is pinned by the tests — along with every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the modules' own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. The byte form gives byte `b` the bits `8b` through `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, so a byte carries every one of its eight bits and the whole set survives a trip through `toBytes` and `fromBytes`.

The Bloom filter derives two 32-bit hashes from a value and its seed and probes `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits` for each of its `hashes` rounds. Those hashes are 32-bit values and the arithmetic that combines them is 32-bit and unsigned: every probe must land on a valid bit index for any input. A value that was added is always reported as present. `union` merges two filters only when they agree on their bit count, their probe count, and their seed, and refuses otherwise with a `RangeError`. `serialize` writes a four-byte signature, the bit count, the seed, the probe count, the number of added values, and then the bits; `deserialize` restores all of it.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the modules by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

6: /** Error raised for malformed templates and impossible renders. */
7: export class TemplateError extends Error {

21: const ESCAPES = [

156: function owns(frame, key) {

176:     }
177:     return value;
178:   }
179:   return undefined;
180: }

182: /**
183:  * Render a node list against a context stack.
184:  *
185:  * @param {object[]} nodes Nodes to render.
186:  * @param {unknown[]} stack Context frames, innermost first.
187:  * @param {{partials: Record<string, string>, maxDepth: number, depth: number}} state Shared render state.
188:  * @returns {string} Rendered text.
189:  */
190: function renderNodes(nodes, stack, state) {
191:   let output = '';
192:   for (const node of nodes) {
193:     if (node.type === 'text') {
194:       output += node.value;
195:       continue;
196:     }
197:     if (node.type === 'variable') {
198:       const text = stringify(resolve(stack, node.name));
199:       output += node.escaped ? escapeHtml(text) : text;
200:       continue;
201:     }
202:     if (node.type === 'section') {
203:       const value = resolve(stack, node.name);
204:       if (node.inverted) {
205:         if (!value) output += renderNodes(node.children, stack, state);
206:         continue;
207:       }
208:       if (isEmpty(value)) continue;
209:       if (Array.isArray(value)) {
210:         for (const item of value) output += renderNodes(node.children, [item, ...stack], state);
211:       } else if (typeof value === 'object') {
212:         output += renderNodes(node.children, [value, ...stack], state);
213:       } else {
214:         output += renderNodes(node.children, stack, state);
215:       }
216:       continue;
217:     }
218:     const source = state.partials[node.name];
219:     if (typeof source !== 'string') {

221:     }
222:     if (state.depth >= state.maxDepth) {

237: function checkOptions(options) {
238:   if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
239:     throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'options must be an object', 0);

241:   const partials = options.partials ?? {};

249:   return { partials, maxDepth, depth: 0 };

257:  */
258: export function compile(template) {
259:   const nodes = parse(template);

All 12 tests pass now. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`escapeHtml` ampersand ordering** — `&` was escaped last, so it would re-escape entities it had just produced (e.g. `<` → `<` → the `&` in that would get escaped too). Moved `&` → `&` to be the first substitution, matching the "escaping is total, so `&` gets escaped again" requirement.

2. **`stringify` swallowed falsy values** — `String(value || '')` turned `0` and `false` into `''` instead of `'0'`/`'false'`. Changed to `String(value)` (guarded above for `null`/`undefined`).

3. **Inverted sections used truthiness instead of `isEmpty`** — `!value` doesn't treat an empty array as empty, so `{{^a}}` over `[]` failed to render its block. Changed to use the same `isEmpty` helper as normal sections.

4. **Partial depth counter never decremented** — `state.depth` was incremented on entering a partial but never decremented after, so sibling partials (not nested) incorrectly accumulated depth and could hit `PARTIAL_DEPTH` prematurely, or a second `compile()`/`render()` call... (actually `checkOptions` resets it each call, but within one render, sibling partials must not stack). Added `state.depth -= 1` after rendering the partial's nodes.

5. **Context stack searched in the wrong order** — `resolve` reversed the stack before searching, but the stack's convention (per the spec and `renderNodes`, which does `[item, ...stack]`) is innermost-first already. Reversing made it search outermost-first, breaking scoping (`{{#xs}}{{name}}{{/xs}}` returned the outer name instead of the inner one). Removed the `.reverse()` so it searches the stack in its natural innermost-first order.

The public exports (`TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile`, `render`) are unchanged, only internal logic was corrected, and no dependencies or files outside `src/` were touched.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/query-string.js` is a finished reader and writer for URL query strings, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `stringify` and `extract`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(input, options)` reads a query string, with or without a leading `?` or `#`, into an object. Pairs are separated by `&`, empty pairs are skipped, and each pair splits at its first unencoded `=`, with a missing `=` meaning an empty value. Keys and values are decoded separately: `+` stands for a space unless `options.plusAsSpace` is false, percent escapes are decoded, and text that cannot be decoded is kept as it is. A key is split into a path on its unencoded brackets before any decoding, so `a[b][c]` nests but an encoded bracket stays part of a name; `options.depth` (5 by default) limits how many bracket groups are structural, and whatever is left of the key becomes one final literal segment. Empty brackets append to the container, a repeated plain key collects its values into an array in order, and a container whose keys are all non-negative integers written without leading zeros becomes an array, ordered by index with missing indices dropped, as long as the largest index is below `options.arrayLimit` (20 by default). Every key is stored as an own property, so `__proto__` never reaches a prototype, and each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence.

`stringify(input, options)` writes an object back. Members are written in insertion order, or ordered by their whole written key when `options.sort` is true, comparing by code unit. A nested object writes `a[b]=x`; an array writes `a[0]=x` by default, `a[]=x` under `arrayFormat: 'brackets'` and `a=x` under `arrayFormat: 'repeat'`; an empty array or object writes nothing. Strings, numbers and booleans become their text, `undefined` members are skipped, and a `null` member writes its key with no `=` at all unless `options.skipNull` is set, which drops it. Keys and values are percent-encoded, including `!'()*`, with structural brackets left literal and spaces written as `%20` or, under `space: 'plus'`, as `+`. `extract(url)` returns the text after the first `?` that comes before any `#`, or the empty string. Bad arguments throw `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. 1: /**
2:  * URL query string reader and writer with bracket-nested keys, arrays,
3:  * percent-encoding and stable ordering.
4:  *
5:  * Keys are split on unencoded brackets before anything is decoded, so a key
6:  * that contains an encoded bracket stays one name, and a value that contains an
7:  * encoded `=` stays one value.
8:  */
9: 
10: const DEFAULT_DEPTH = 5;
11: const DEFAULT_ARRAY_LIMIT = 20;
12: const ARRAY_FORMATS = new Set(['indices', 'brackets', 'repeat']);
13: const INTEGER = /^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/;
14: const EXTRA_ENCODED = /[!'()*]/g;
15: 
16: /** Marker for an empty bracket group, which appends instead of naming a member. */
17: const PUSH = Symbol('push');
18: 
19: /** Results already produced for a query string. */
20: const parsed = new Map();
21: 
22: /**
23:  * Store an own, enumerable property even when the key shadows `Object.prototype`.
24:  *
25:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} target object to write into
26:  * @param {string} key property name
27:  * @param {unknown} value property value
28:  * @returns {void}
29:  */
30: function setOwn(target, key, value) {
31:   Object.defineProperty(target, key, { value, writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true });
32: }
33: 
34: /**
35:  * Decode one key or value component.
36:  *
37:  * @param {string} text raw component text
38:  * @param {boolean} plusAsSpace whether `+` stands for a space
39:  * @returns {string} the decoded text, or the undecoded text when the escapes are malformed
40:  */
41: function decodeComponent(text, plusAsSpace) {
42:   const spaced = plusAsSpace ? text.split('+').join(' ') : text;
43:   try {
44:     return decodeURIComponent(spaced);
45:   } catch {
46:     return spaced;
47:   }
48: }
49: 
50: /**
51:  * Split one `key=value` segment at its first unencoded `=`.
52:  *
53:  * @param {string} segment raw segment text
54:  * @returns {{ rawKey: string, rawValue: string }} the two halves, still encoded
55:  */
56: function splitPair(segment) {
57:   const at = segment.indexOf('=');
58:   if (at === -1) return { rawKey: segment, rawValue: '' };
59:   return { rawKey: segment.slice(0, at), rawValue: segment.slice(at + 1) };
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Split a raw key into decoded path segments on its unencoded brackets.
64:  *
65:  * @param {string} rawKey raw key text
66:  * @param {number} depth how many bracket groups are structural
67:  * @param {boolean} plusAsSpace whether `+` stands for a space
68:  * @returns {(string | symbol)[]} the path, starting with the base name, with a marker for each empty bracket group
69:  */
70: function keyPath(rawKey, depth, plusAsSpace) {
71:   const key = decodeComponent(rawKey, plusAsSpace);
72:   const open = key.indexOf('[');
73:   if (open === -1) return [key];
74: 
75:   const segments = [key.slice(0, open)];
76:   let i = open;
77:   while (i < key.length && segments.length <= depth) {
78:     if (key[i] !== '[') break;
79:     const close = key.indexOf(']', i);
80:     if (close === -1) break;
81:     const inner = key.slice(i + 1, close);
82:     segments.push(inner === '' ? PUSH : inner);
83:     i = close + 1;
84:   }
85:   if (i < key.length) segments.push(key.slice(i));
86:   return segments;
87: }
88: 
89: /**
90:  * The index an empty bracket group appends at.
91:  *
92:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} node container to append to
93:  * @returns {number} one past the highest integer key, or 0 when there is none
94:  */
95: function nextIndex(node) {
96:   let highest = -1;
97:   for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
98:     if (INTEGER.test(key)) highest = Math.max(highest, Number(key));
99:   }
100:   return highest + 1;
101: }
102: 
103: /**
104:  * Whether a value is a container the walk can descend into.
105:  *
106:  * @param {unknown} value value to classify
107:  * @returns {boolean} true for a non-null object
108:  */
109: function isContainer(value) {
110:   return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null;
111: }
112: 
113: /**
114:  * Record one decoded pair in the working tree.
115:  *
116:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} root working tree
117:  * @param {string[]} path decoded key path
118:  * @param {string} value decoded value
119:  * @returns {void}
120:  */
121: function assign(root, path, value) {
122:   let node = root;
123:   for (let i = 0; i < path.length - 1; i += 1) {
124:     const key = path[i] === PUSH ? String(nextIndex(node)) : path[i];
125:     const existing = Object.hasOwn(node, key) ? node[key] : undefined;
126:     if (isContainer(existing) && !Array.isArray(existing)) {
127:       node = existing;
128:       continue;
129:     }
130:     const created = {};
131:     setOwn(node, key, created);
132:     node = created;
133:   }
134: 
135:   const last = path[path.length - 1];
136:   if (last === PUSH) {
137:     setOwn(node, String(nextIndex(node)), value);
138:     return;
139:   }
140:   if (!Object.hasOwn(node, last)) {
141:     setOwn(node, last, value);
142:     return;
143:   }
144:   const existing = node[last];
145:   if (Array.isArray(existing)) {
146:     existing.push(value);
147:     return;
148:   }
149:   if (isContainer(existing)) return;
150:   setOwn(node, last, [existing, value]);
151: }
152: 
153: /**
154:  * Turn integer-keyed containers into arrays, dropping missing indices.
155:  *
156:  * @param {unknown} node value to convert
157:  * @param {number} arrayLimit highest index that still allows an array
158:  * @returns {unknown} the converted value
159:  */
160: function compact(node, arrayLimit) {
161:   if (!isContainer(node) || Array.isArray(node)) return node;
162: 
163:   const keys = Object.keys(node);
164:   const converted = {};
165:   for (const key of keys) setOwn(converted, key, compact(node[key], arrayLimit));
166:   if (keys.length === 0) return converted;
167:   if (!keys.every((key) => INTEGER.test(key))) return converted;
168:   if (Math.max(...keys.map(Number)) > arrayLimit) return converted;
169:   return keys
170:     .slice()
171:     .sort((a, b) => Number(a) - Number(b))
172:     .map((key) => converted[key]);
173: }
174: 
175: /**
176:  * Read a query string.
177:  *
178:  * @param {string} input query text, with or without a leading `?` or `#`
179:  * @param {{ depth?: number, arrayLimit?: number, plusAsSpace?: boolean }} [options] nesting and decoding policy
180:  * @returns {Record<string, unknown>} the decoded parameters
181:  */
182: export function parse(input, options = {}) {
183:   if (typeof input !== 'string') throw new TypeError('input must be a string');
184:   const memoised = parsed.get(input);
185:   if (memoised !== undefined) return memoised;
186:   const depth = options.depth ?? DEFAULT_DEPTH;
187:   const arrayLimit = options.arrayLimit ?? DEFAULT_ARRAY_LIMIT;
188:   const plusAsSpace = options.plusAsSpace !== false;
189: 
190:   const text = input.startsWith('?') || input.startsWith('#') ? input.slice(1) : input;
191:   const tree = {};
192:   for (const segment of text.split('&')) {
193:     if (segment === '') continue;
194:     const { rawKey, rawValue } = splitPair(segment);
195:     assign(tree, keyPath(rawKey, depth, options.plusAsSpace === true), decodeComponent(rawValue, plusAsSpace));
196:   }
197: 
198:   const result = {};
199:   for (const key of Object.keys(tree)) setOwn(result, key, compact(tree[key], arrayLimit));
200:   parsed.set(input, result);
201:   return result;
202: }
203: 
204: /**
205:  * Percent-encode one key or value component.
206:  *
207:  * @param {string} text component text
208:  * @param {string} space `'plus'` to write spaces as `+`, `'percent'` otherwise
209:  * @returns {string} the encoded component
210:  */
211: function encodeComponent(text, space) {
212:   const encoded = encodeURIComponent(text).replace(
213:     EXTRA_ENCODED,
214:     (character) => `%${character.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase()}`,
215:   );
216:   return space === 'plus' ? encoded.split('%20').join('+') : encoded;
217: }
218: 
219: /**
220:  * Build the written key for one path.
221:  *
222:  * @param {string[]} segments key path
223:  * @param {string} space space-encoding policy
224:  * @returns {string} the encoded key, with structural brackets left literal
225:  */
226: function keyText(segments, space) {
227:   let out = encodeComponent(segments[0], space);
228:   for (const segment of segments.slice(1)) out += `[${encodeComponent(segment, space)}]`;
229:   return out;
230: }
231: 
232: /**
233:  * Walk one value, appending the pairs it produces.
234:  *
235:  * @param {string[]} segments key path so far
236:  * @param {unknown} value value to write
237:  * @param {{ path: string, value: string | null }[]} pairs accumulated pairs
238:  * @param {{ arrayFormat: string, skipNull: boolean, space: string }} options writing policy
239:  * @returns {void}
240:  */
241: function collect(segments, value, pairs, options) {
242:   if (value === undefined || typeof value === 'function' || typeof value === 'symbol') return;
243: 
244:   if (value === null) {
245:     if (options.skipNull) return;
246:     pairs.push({ path: keyText(segments, options.space), value: '' });
247:     return;
248:   }
249: 
250:   if (Array.isArray(value)) {
251:     for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i += 1) {
252:       if (options.arrayFormat === 'repeat') collect(segments, value[i], pairs, options);
253:       else collect([...segments, options.arrayFormat === 'brackets' ? '' : String(i)], value[i], pairs, options);
254:     }
255:     return;
256:   }
257: 
258:   if (isContainer(value)) {
259:     for (const key of Object.keys(value)) collect([...segments, key], value[key], pairs, options);
260:     return;
261:   }
262: 
263:   pairs.push({ path: keyText(segments, options.space), value: encodeComponent(String(value), options.space) });
264: }

266: /**
267:  * Write a query string.
268:  *
269:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} input parameters to write
270:  * @param {{ arrayFormat?: string, sort?: boolean, skipNull?: boolean, space?: string }} [options] writing policy
271:  * @returns {string} the query text, without a leading `?`
272:  */
273: export function stringify(input, options = {}) {
274:   if (!isContainer(input) || Array.isArray(input)) throw new TypeError('input must be an object');
275:   const arrayFormat = options.arrayFormat ?? 'indices';
276:   if (!ARRAY_FORMATS.has(arrayFormat)) throw new TypeError(`unknown arrayFormat: ${arrayFormat}`);
277:   const space = options.space ?? 'percent';
278:   if (space !== 'percent' && space !== 'plus') throw new TypeError(`unknown space: ${space}`);
279: 
280:   const policy = { arrayFormat, skipNull: options.skipNull === true, space };
281:   const pairs = [];
282:   for (const key of Object.keys(input)) collect([key], input[key], pairs, policy);
283:   if (options.sort === true) {
284:     pairs.sort((left, right) => {
285:       if (left.path === right.path) return 0;
286:       return left.path < right.path ? -1 : 1;
287:     });
288:   }
289:   return pairs.map((pair) => (pair.value === null ? pair.path : `${pair.path}=${pair.value}`)).join('&');
290: }
291:

293:  * Take the query part out of a URL.
294:  *
295:  * @param {string} url URL or URL fragment
296:  * @returns {string} the text after the first `?` that precedes any `#`, or the empty string

12:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;

content.text:
I've identified all the bugs. Let me fix them:

1. **Memoization cache bug**: `parsed` Map is keyed only by `input`, ignoring `options`, and returns the *same* mutable object across calls — violating "each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence" and causing both the depth-reuse bug and the mutation-leak bug.
2. **`keyPath` decodes before splitting**: it decodes the whole raw key first, then splits on brackets — so percent-encoded brackets get treated as structural. Must split on raw text first, then decode each segment.
3. **Wrong `plusAsSpace` passed to `keyPath`**: `options.plusAsSpace === true` instead of the computed `plusAsSpace` (default `true`).
4. **`compact` array-limit check uses `>` instead of `>=`**: spec says index must be *below* `arrayLimit`.
5. **`stringify` for `null` writes `value: ''`** instead of `null`, producing `a=` instead of `a`.

All 14 tests now pass (14/14, 0 failures). Here's a summary of the faults found and fixed in `src/query-string.js`:

1. **Cross-call state leak (`parsed` Map cache)** — `parse` memoized results by `input` text alone, ignoring `options`, and handed back the *same* mutable object on repeated calls. This broke the "each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence" guarantee and caused stale results when `depth`/`arrayLimit` differed between calls with the same input. Removed the cache entirely.

2. **Keys decoded before bracket-splitting** — `keyPath` called `decodeComponent` on the *whole* raw key before looking for `[`/`]`, so a percent-encoded bracket (e.g. `a%5Bb%5D`) got treated as structural nesting instead of staying part of the literal name. Fixed by splitting on brackets in the raw (undecoded) text first, then decoding each resulting segment independently.

3. **Wrong `plusAsSpace` flag threaded into key decoding** — `parse` passed `options.plusAsSpace === true` into `keyPath` instead of the computed default-true `plusAsSpace` value, so `+` wasn't treated as a space in keys unless `plusAsSpace` was explicitly set. Fixed to pass the correctly computed flag.

4. **Off-by-one in the array-limit check** — `compact` converted a container to an array unless `Math.max(index) > arrayLimit`, but the spec requires the largest index to be *below* `arrayLimit` (strict). Changed the comparison to `>=`.

5. **`null` values stringified as empty strings** — `collect` pushed `{ value: '' }` for `null` members, causing `stringify({ a: null })` to write `a=` instead of the bare key `a`. Changed to push `{ value: null }` so the final join correctly omits the `=`.

With these five fixes, all previously-passing behaviors are preserved and the previously-failing cases (encoded brackets, `+` in keys, array-limit boundary, depth reuse, memoized mutation leakage, null stringification, and the randomized round-trip test) now pass.

`src/query-string.js` is a finished reader and writer for URL query strings, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `stringify` and `extract`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(input, options)` reads a query string, with or without a leading `?` or `#`, into an object. Pairs are separated by `&`, empty pairs are skipped, and each pair splits at its first unencoded `=`, with a missing `=` meaning an empty value. Keys and values are decoded separately: `+` stands for a space unless `options.plusAsSpace` is false, percent escapes are decoded, and text that cannot be decoded is kept as it is. A key is split into a path on its unencoded brackets before any decoding, so `a[b][c]` nests but an encoded bracket stays part of a name; `options.depth` (5 by default) limits how many bracket groups are structural, and whatever is left of the key becomes one final literal segment. Empty brackets append to the container, a repeated plain key collects its values into an array in order, and a container whose keys are all non-negative integers written without leading zeros becomes an array, ordered by index with missing indices dropped, as long as the largest index is below `options.arrayLimit` (20 by default). Every key is stored as an own property, so `__proto__` never reaches a prototype, and each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence.

`stringify(input, options)` writes an object back. Members are written in insertion order, or ordered by their whole written key when `options.sort` is true, comparing by code unit. A nested object writes `a[b]=x`; an array writes `a[0]=x` by default, `a[]=x` under `arrayFormat: 'brackets'` and `a=x` under `arrayFormat: 'repeat'`; an empty array or object writes nothing. Strings, numbers and booleans become their text, `undefined` members are skipped, and a `null` member writes its key with no `=` at all unless `options.skipNull` is set, which drops it. Keys and values are percent-encoded, including `!'()*`, with structural brackets left literal and spaces written as `%20` or, under `space: 'plus'`, as `+`. `extract(url)` returns the text after the first `?` that comes before any `#`, or the empty string. Bad arguments throw `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

All 15 tests now pass. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`#dependenciesSatisfied`**: was checking `status !== 'pending'`, which incorrectly treated `running`, `cancelled`, `missed`, and `blocked` dependencies as satisfied. Fixed to require `status === 'done'`.

2. **`#blockDependents`**: the transitive block queue never pushed newly-blocked jobs onto `queue`, so blocking only cascaded one level deep instead of all the way down. Added `queue.push(job.id)` when a job becomes blocked.

3. **`cancel(id)`**: only refused to cancel `running` jobs, but should refuse for anything that isn't `pending` (already cancelled, missed, or blocked jobs should return `false` and be left alone). Fixed the guard to `job.status !== 'pending'`.

4. **`compareJobs`**: compared `deadlineMs` before `priority`, but the spec requires priority to be the primary sort key, deadline the tiebreaker, then id. Swapped the order.

5. **Deadline check in `#startEligible`**: used `now >= job.deadlineMs` to decide a miss, which incorrectly missed jobs starting exactly on their deadline. Spec says a job starting exactly at its deadline should still run. Fixed to `now > job.deadlineMs`.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

14: const EXTRA_ENCODED = /[!'()*]/g;

24:  *
25:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} target object to write into

27:  * @param {unknown} value property value
28:  * @returns {void}

38:  * @param {boolean} plusAsSpace whether `+` stands for a space

43:   try {
44:     return decodeURIComponent(spaced);

All 14 tests in `test/query-string.test.js` now pass, and `node_modules` was not created. Here's a summary of the faults I found and fixed in `src/query-string.js`:

1. **Keys were decoded before splitting on brackets** — `keyPath` called `decodeComponent` on the whole raw key up front, so an encoded bracket (`%5B`/`%5D`) turned into a literal `[`/`]` and got treated as structural nesting instead of staying part of a literal name (e.g. `a%5Bb%5D=c` wrongly became `{a:{b:'c'}}` instead of `{'a[b]':'c'}`). This also meant `+` in a bracket segment was decoded even when it shouldn't be tied to that path's semantics correctly. Fixed by splitting the raw (still-encoded) key on unencoded `[`/`]` first, and decoding each resulting segment individually afterward.

2. **`plusAsSpace` was applied inconsistently to keys** — the call site passed `options.plusAsSpace === true` (default `false`) into `keyPath` instead of the already-computed `plusAsSpace` value (default `true`), inverting the default behavior for keys (e.g. `a+b=c+d` failed to turn `+` into a space in the key). Fixed by passing the correctly computed `plusAsSpace` through.

3. **Off-by-one in the array-limit check** — `compact` used `Math.max(...indices) > arrayLimit` instead of `>= arrayLimit`, so an index equal to the limit (e.g. index `20` with default limit `20`) was incorrectly still converted to an array rather than staying an object. Fixed the comparison to `>=`.

4. **`null` values in `stringify` were written as `key=` instead of bare `key`** — `collect` pushed `value: ''` for `null` members, and the final join always wrote `=value`. Fixed by pushing `value: null` as the marker, which the existing join logic (`pair.value === null ? pair.path : ...`) already correctly renders as the bare key.

5. **Unwanted cross-call memoization in `parse`** — a module-level `parsed` Map cached results by input string and returned the *same* object/array references on repeated calls, which violated "each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence" (mutating one parse result corrupted subsequent calls with the same input). Removed the memoization entirely so every call builds a fresh tree.

All fixes were confined to `src/query-string.js`; no test files, `package.json`, or dependencies were touched, and no special-casing of specific test inputs was introduced — each fix addresses a general logic error per the spec.

goal.objective:
`src/query-string.js` is a finished reader and writer for URL query strings, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `stringify` and `extract`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(input, options)` reads a query string, with or without a leading `?` or `#`, into an object. Pairs are separated by `&`, empty pairs are skipped, and each pair splits at its first unencoded `=`, with a missing `=` meaning an empty value. Keys and values are decoded separately: `+` stands for a space unless `options.plusAsSpace` is false, percent escapes are decoded, and text that cannot be decoded is kept as it is. A key is split into a path on its unencoded brackets before any decoding, so `a[b][c]` nests but an encoded bracket stays part of a name; `options.depth` (5 by default) limits how many bracket groups are structural, and whatever is left of the key becomes one final literal segment. Empty brackets append to the container, a repeated plain key collects its values into an array in order, and a container whose keys are all non-negative integers written without leading zeros becomes an array, ordered by index with missing indices dropped, as long as the largest index is below `options.arrayLimit` (20 by default). Every key is stored as an own property, so `__proto__` never reaches a prototype, and each call returns a result no earlier call can observe or influence.

`stringify(input, options)` writes an object back. Members are written in insertion order, or ordered by their whole written key when `options.sort` is true, comparing by code unit. A nested object writes `a[b]=x`; an array writes `a[0]=x` by default, `a[]=x` under `arrayFormat: 'brackets'` and `a=x` under `arrayFormat: 'repeat'`; an empty array or object writes nothing. Strings, numbers and booleans become their text, `undefined` members are skipped, and a `null` member writes its key with no `=` at all unless `options.skipNull` is set, which drops it. Keys and values are percent-encoded, including `!'()*`, with structural brackets left literal and spaces written as `%20` or, under `space: 'plus'`, as `+`. `extract(url)` returns the text after the first `?` that comes before any `#`, or the empty string. Bad arguments throw `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

content.text:
`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

All 12 tests pass now. Summary of the faults found and fixed in `src/markdown-inline.js`:

1. **Double percent-encoding of existing triplets** — `encodeDestination` prepended `%25` to already-valid percent-triplets (turning `%20` into `%2520`) instead of leaving them exactly as-is. Fixed to reuse the literal `%` unchanged.

2. **Email autolink regex missing `+`** — `AUTOLINK_EMAIL`'s local-part character class omitted `+`, so addresses like `a+b@example.com` failed to match and fell through to plain escaped text. Added `+` to the class.

Swapped the marker check from `'*'` to `'_'` in both functions.

`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
